explanations.D: Contradicts the stimulus — publication follows, not precedes, legal effect.
explanations.E: Reversal — the stimulus requires Gazette publication for laws, not the converse.

lr.difficultyReason: A rule-plus-exception pattern supports a single-step contrapositive-style inference about a named case.
lr.stimulus: In the Panzar language, every verb that ends in the suffix '-eko' takes its past tense by adding '-ta'. The only exceptions are verbs whose stem ends in a vowel; those instead take '-nta'. The Panzar verb 'sareko' has a stem ending in the consonant 'r'.
lr.questionStem: If the statements above are true, which one of the following must also be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The past tense of 'sareko' is formed by adding '-ta'.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Most Panzar verbs end in the suffix '-eko'.

choices.label: C
choices.text: No Panzar verb ending in '-eko' has a stem ending in a vowel.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Any Panzar verb taking '-nta' in the past tense ends in '-eko'.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The past tense of 'sareko' is 'sareko-nta'.

explanations.correct: 'sareko' ends in '-eko' and its stem ends in a consonant, so it does not fall under the vowel-stem exception. Therefore it follows the default rule: add '-ta'.
explanations.A: Correct.
explanations.B: Unsupported — the stimulus gives no information about the relative frequency of '-eko' verbs.
explanations.C: Contradicts the stimulus — the exception clause asserts that some '-eko' verbs do have vowel-final stems.
explanations.D: Reversal — '-nta' applies to vowel-stem '-eko' verbs, not uniquely so as far as the stimulus tells us.
explanations.E: Contradicts the inference — 'sareko' has a consonant stem, so it takes '-ta', not '-nta'.

lr.difficultyReason: Requires chaining a universal conditional with an existential claim and applying the contrapositive. Trap (A) inverts the conditional; trap (D) converts 'some' into 'most.'
lr.stimulus: Every drug that has received expedited regulatory review in the past decade has been developed by a company with in-house clinical trial capacity. Some drugs developed by companies with in-house clinical trial capacity have later been withdrawn from the market because of safety concerns. No drug that was developed exclusively by an outside contract research organization has received expedited review.
lr.questionStem: If the statements above are true, which one of the following must also be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Any drug developed by a company with in-house clinical trial capacity has received expedited regulatory review.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Most drugs that have received expedited regulatory review have been withdrawn from the market because of safety concerns.

choices.label: C
choices.text: At least some drugs developed by companies with in-house clinical trial capacity have been withdrawn from the market because of safety concerns.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Most drugs developed exclusively by outside contract research organizations have been withdrawn from the market.

choices.label: E
choices.text: No drug that has been withdrawn for safety concerns has received expedited regulatory review.

explanations.correct: The second sentence states directly that some drugs developed by companies with in-house trial capacity have been withdrawn for safety concerns. (C) simply restates that existential claim using the hedged 'at least some,' which follows trivially.
explanations.A: Inverts the conditional. 'Every expedited drug has in-house capacity' does not entail that every in-house drug received expedited review.
explanations.B: Collapses 'some' into 'most.' The stimulus supports only that some withdrawals came from in-house developers, not that most expedited drugs were withdrawn.
explanations.C: Correct.
explanations.D: Out of scope and overreaching — the stimulus says nothing about the fate of drugs developed exclusively by contract research organizations.
explanations.E: Could be true but not must. Some in-house-developed expedited drugs may have been withdrawn for safety reasons; the passage does not preclude that.

lr.difficultyReason: Requires chaining two conditionals and applying the contrapositive of the second. Trap (B) is the converse error; trap (E) overreaches to a universal.
lr.stimulus: All of the paintings in the Harwell Gallery's permanent collection were acquired before 1950. Any painting acquired before 1950 that has been exhibited in the last ten years has undergone conservation treatment. The gallery's painting 'Marsh at Dusk' has not undergone conservation treatment. 'Marsh at Dusk' is part of the gallery's permanent collection.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following must be true on the basis of the statements above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: 'Marsh at Dusk' has not been exhibited in the last ten years.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Any painting in the gallery's permanent collection that has undergone conservation treatment has been exhibited in the last ten years.

choices.label: C
choices.text: 'Marsh at Dusk' was acquired after 1950.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Most paintings in the permanent collection have been exhibited in the last ten years.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Every painting acquired before 1950 has undergone conservation treatment.

explanations.correct: Because 'Marsh at Dusk' is in the permanent collection, it was acquired before 1950. The conditional then says any such painting that has been exhibited in the last ten years has been conserved. By contrapositive, a pre-1950 painting that has not been conserved has not been exhibited in the last ten years. That applies to 'Marsh at Dusk.'
explanations.A: Correct.
explanations.B: Inverts the conditional. The rule goes from 'exhibited' to 'conserved,' not the other way.
explanations.C: Contradicted by the stimulus — permanent-collection paintings were all acquired before 1950.
explanations.D: Could be true but not must. The stimulus gives no distribution of exhibited vs. unexhibited works.
explanations.E: Overreach. The conditional applies only to pre-1950 paintings that have been exhibited in the last ten years, not all pre-1950 paintings.

lr.difficultyReason: Requires combining a universal claim with a most-statement to derive a guaranteed existential overlap. Trap (C) collapses 'most' into 'all'; trap (D) is a could-be-true.
lr.stimulus: Every member of the Riverton Medical Society holds an active license to practice medicine in the state. Most members of the Riverton Medical Society have completed a residency in internal medicine. A few members of the society practice exclusively in rural clinics outside Riverton.
lr.questionStem: If the statements above are true, which one of the following must also be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Most licensed physicians in the state are members of the Riverton Medical Society.

choices.label: B
choices.text: At least some members of the society who completed an internal medicine residency hold an active state medical license.

choices.label: C
choices.text: All members of the society have completed a residency in internal medicine.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Some members of the society who practice in rural clinics have completed a residency in internal medicine.

choices.label: E
choices.text: No member of the society who lacks an internal medicine residency practices in a rural clinic.

explanations.correct: Every member of the society holds an active license. Most members have completed an internal medicine residency — those members are also members, so they also hold the license. Hence at least some (in fact all) members who completed the residency hold a license.
explanations.A: Out of scope. The stimulus doesn't address what share of state physicians belong to the society.
explanations.B: Correct.
explanations.C: Collapses 'most' into 'all.' The stimulus supports only that most, not all, members completed an internal medicine residency.
explanations.D: Could be true but not must. 'Most' and 'a few' can overlap, but the stimulus does not force overlap.
explanations.E: Could be true but not must. Nothing forbids a rural-clinic member who did not complete an internal medicine residency.

lr.difficultyReason: Requires applying the contrapositive of a two-variable conditional and rejecting a converse trap. Trap (A) affirms the consequent; trap (E) is too strong.
lr.stimulus: If a manufacturing firm in this region has reduced its energy costs by more than 20 percent over the past five years, then it has either installed on-site solar generation or switched to a regional renewable electricity supplier. The Farley Plant has neither installed on-site solar generation nor switched to a regional renewable electricity supplier. Every manufacturing firm in this region that has switched to a regional renewable electricity supplier has signed a long-term fixed-rate contract.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following must be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Any manufacturing firm in the region that has installed on-site solar generation has reduced its energy costs by more than 20 percent over the past five years.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Farley Plant has not reduced its energy costs by more than 20 percent over the past five years.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Farley Plant has signed a long-term fixed-rate contract.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Most manufacturing firms in the region have reduced their energy costs by more than 20 percent.

choices.label: E
choices.text: No manufacturing firm in the region has reduced its energy costs without switching to a regional renewable electricity supplier.

explanations.correct: The first sentence says a firm with greater-than-20% cost reduction must have done one of the two listed things. By contrapositive, a firm that has done neither cannot have reduced its costs by more than 20%. That's the Farley Plant.
explanations.A: Affirms the consequent. The conditional runs from cost reduction to action, not from action to cost reduction.
explanations.B: Correct.
explanations.C: Could be true but not must. The fixed-rate rule applies only to firms that switched suppliers, and Farley did not.
explanations.D: Unsupported. The stimulus gives no distributional claim about manufacturing firms generally.
explanations.E: Overreach — the first sentence lists two alternatives, so cost reduction doesn't require supplier switching specifically.

lr.difficultyReason: Requires reading 'unless' correctly and chaining it with a second conditional. Trap (B) is a temporal-confusion overreach; trap (E) collapses 'some' into 'all.'
lr.stimulus: No historical monograph published by the Brindle University Press is accepted for publication unless it has been reviewed by at least two outside specialists. Some historical monographs that have been reviewed by at least two outside specialists are rejected on grounds of insufficient archival evidence. Every historical monograph that is rejected on grounds of insufficient archival evidence can be resubmitted after further archival research.
lr.questionStem: If the statements above are true, which one of the following must also be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: At least some historical monographs that have been reviewed by two outside specialists can be resubmitted after further archival research.

choices.label: B
choices.text: No historical monograph submitted to the Brindle University Press is rejected for any reason other than insufficient archival evidence.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Any historical monograph that is reviewed by at least two outside specialists is eventually accepted for publication.

choices.label: D
choices.text: All historical monographs published by the Brindle University Press have been resubmitted at least once.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Every historical monograph submitted to the press has been reviewed by at least two outside specialists.

explanations.correct: The stimulus says some monographs reviewed by two or more specialists are rejected for insufficient archival evidence, and every such rejected monograph can be resubmitted. Chaining these yields: some monographs reviewed by two or more specialists can be resubmitted.
explanations.A: Correct.
explanations.B: Out of scope. The stimulus lists one ground for rejection but does not say it is the only one.
explanations.C: Contradicted by the stimulus — some reviewed monographs are rejected.
explanations.D: Overreach. The stimulus permits resubmission but does not claim published monographs were in fact resubmitted.
explanations.E: Inverts the 'unless' clause. The rule says reviewing is necessary for acceptance, not for submission.

lr.difficultyReason: Requires chaining a universal with a most-claim via a common subject to guarantee existential overlap. Trap (D) is the converse; trap (C) is too strong.
lr.stimulus: All tenured professors at Kirchner College serve on at least one standing committee. Most tenured professors at Kirchner College are also members of the Faculty Senate. Every member of the Faculty Senate has voting privileges on curricular matters.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following must be true on the basis of the statements above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Every tenured professor at Kirchner College has voting privileges on curricular matters.

choices.label: B
choices.text: At least some tenured professors at Kirchner College who serve on a standing committee have voting privileges on curricular matters.

choices.label: C
choices.text: All members of the Faculty Senate are tenured professors at Kirchner College.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Any professor at Kirchner College who has voting privileges on curricular matters is a tenured professor.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Most members of the Faculty Senate serve on more than one standing committee.

explanations.correct: Most tenured professors are Faculty Senate members (so at least some exist); every such Senate member has curricular voting privileges; and every tenured professor serves on at least one standing committee. Therefore at least some tenured professors who serve on a standing committee have curricular voting privileges.
explanations.A: Overreach — only the tenured professors who are Senate members are guaranteed voting privileges, and 'most' is not 'all.'
explanations.B: Correct.
explanations.C: Converse error — Senate members need not be tenured professors.
explanations.D: Converse error — curricular voting privileges may extend to non-tenured Senate members.
explanations.E: Unsupported. The stimulus says nothing about how many committees Senate members serve on.

lr.difficultyReason: Requires pairing a universal claim with a specific instance to derive a conditional about a named subject. Trap (A) overreaches by generalizing to all soils; trap (E) introduces scope shift.
lr.stimulus: Any agricultural soil in the Mendris Valley with a pH below 5.8 has measurable concentrations of aluminum that inhibit wheat root development. Soils that inhibit wheat root development cannot support commercially viable wheat yields without amendment. The east parcel of the Dahl farm has an agricultural soil in the Mendris Valley with a pH of 5.4.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following must be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: All agricultural soils in the Mendris Valley require amendment to support commercially viable wheat yields.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The soil on the east parcel of the Dahl farm cannot support commercially viable wheat yields without amendment.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Most farms in the Mendris Valley have soils with a pH below 5.8.

choices.label: D
choices.text: If a soil's pH is above 5.8, it will support commercially viable wheat yields without amendment.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The east parcel of the Dahl farm has the lowest soil pH in the Mendris Valley.

explanations.correct: The east parcel's soil has pH 5.4, below 5.8. By the first conditional, it inhibits wheat root development. By the second, it cannot support commercially viable wheat yields without amendment.
explanations.A: Overreach — the rule applies only to Mendris Valley soils with pH below 5.8, not all valley soils.
explanations.B: Correct.
explanations.C: Unsupported — the stimulus gives no distribution of valley soil pH.
explanations.D: Negates the antecedent — a pH above 5.8 doesn't guarantee viability, since other amendments may still be needed.
explanations.E: Scope shift — the stimulus does not compare pH across parcels.

lr.difficultyReason: Requires combining two universals about overlapping groups to force an existential intersection. Trap (A) is the converse; trap (B) is could-be-true.
lr.stimulus: Every person who serves on the city's zoning board must also hold membership in the local bar association. Some members of the local bar association have represented clients in disputes before the zoning board. No person who has represented a client in a dispute before the zoning board in the past two years may serve on the zoning board.
lr.questionStem: If the statements above are true, which one of the following must also be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Every member of the local bar association is eligible to serve on the city's zoning board.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Some members of the local bar association who have represented clients before the zoning board are currently serving on it.

choices.label: C
choices.text: No member of the zoning board has represented a client in a dispute before the board in the past two years.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Most members of the local bar association have represented clients in disputes before the zoning board.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Anyone who has ever represented a client in a dispute before the zoning board is barred from the bar association.

explanations.correct: The third sentence states that no one who has represented a client before the board in the past two years may serve on it. Since current board members serve on it, none of them can fall in that class.
explanations.A: Converse error — the rule is that board members must be bar members, not that every bar member is eligible.
explanations.B: Contradicted by the stimulus — recent representation disqualifies service.
explanations.C: Correct.
explanations.D: Collapses 'some' into 'most.' The stimulus supports only that some bar members have represented such clients.
explanations.E: Overreach — the stimulus bars certain representers from the zoning board, not from the bar association itself.

lr.difficultyReason: Requires chaining an 'only if' conditional with a contrapositive applied to a specific device. Trap (D) is the converse; trap (E) overreaches on distribution.
lr.stimulus: A consumer electronics device is certified as energy efficient by the Vadren Standards Board only if it consumes less than 0.5 watts in standby mode. Any device that consumes less than 0.5 watts in standby mode uses a modern low-leakage power supply. The Luma-7 home router consumes 1.2 watts in standby mode.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following must be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Luma-7 home router is not certified as energy efficient by the Vadren Standards Board.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Luma-7 home router does not use a modern low-leakage power supply.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Any device that uses a modern low-leakage power supply is certified as energy efficient by the Vadren Standards Board.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Any device that consumes less than 0.5 watts in standby mode is certified as energy efficient by the Vadren Standards Board.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Most home routers are not certified as energy efficient by the Vadren Standards Board.

explanations.correct: 'Certified only if consumes less than 0.5 watts' means certification requires sub-0.5-watt standby. The Luma-7 consumes 1.2 watts — above the threshold — so by contrapositive it is not certified.
explanations.A: Correct.
explanations.B: Could be true but not must. The second rule tells us sub-0.5-watt devices use low-leakage supplies; it doesn't tell us that above-0.5-watt devices can't.
explanations.C: Converse error — low-leakage supply doesn't guarantee certification.
explanations.D: Affirms the necessary condition as if it were sufficient. Sub-0.5-watt standby is necessary for certification but not stated to be sufficient.
explanations.E: Unsupported. The stimulus gives no distribution over home routers.

lr.difficultyReason: Requires applying the contrapositive to a conjunctive consequent, recognizing that failure of one conjunct suffices. Trap (C) is a converse error; trap (E) is could-be-true.
lr.stimulus: Any language that develops a grammatical case system also develops a corresponding set of morphological markers and a stable word order. Proto-Lerian had a well-documented set of morphological markers but no stable word order. Every language descended from Proto-Lerian inherited at least some of its morphological markers.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following must be true on the basis of the statements above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Proto-Lerian did not develop a grammatical case system.

choices.label: B
choices.text: No language descended from Proto-Lerian has a grammatical case system.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Any language with a stable word order and morphological markers develops a grammatical case system.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Most languages descended from Proto-Lerian have a stable word order.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Proto-Lerian's morphological markers originated in an earlier language with a grammatical case system.

explanations.correct: The first sentence requires that a language with a grammatical case system have both morphological markers and a stable word order. Proto-Lerian lacks the latter, so by contrapositive it did not develop a grammatical case system.
explanations.A: Correct.
explanations.B: Overreach. The stimulus is silent on whether descendant languages have developed stable word order and case systems of their own.
explanations.C: Converse error — the conditional runs from case system to the two features, not the other way.
explanations.D: Unsupported. The stimulus says descendants inherited some morphological markers, not that they have stable word order.
explanations.E: Could be true but not must. Nothing in the stimulus establishes how Proto-Lerian's markers originated.

lr.difficultyReason: Requires chaining four conditionals and applying two contrapositives to reach the inference about a named individual. Trap (A) is an affirming-the-consequent error; trap (D) collapses a 'some' into a universal.
lr.stimulus: Every endocrinologist at Meridian Hospital who supervises a first-year resident serves on at least one departmental committee. Any physician at Meridian who serves on a departmental committee has completed the hospital's peer-review training. No physician at Meridian who has completed the peer-review training has fewer than five years of post-fellowship experience. Dr. Ahmadi is an endocrinologist at Meridian with only three years of post-fellowship experience.
lr.questionStem: If the statements above are true, which one of the following must also be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Any endocrinologist at Meridian with at least five years of post-fellowship experience supervises a first-year resident.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Dr. Ahmadi does not supervise a first-year resident.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Dr. Ahmadi has not completed the hospital's peer-review training, and she is therefore ineligible to do so.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Every physician at Meridian who has supervised a first-year resident has at least five years of post-fellowship experience.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Most endocrinologists at Meridian serve on a departmental committee.

explanations.correct: If Dr. Ahmadi supervised a first-year resident, she would (i) serve on a departmental committee, (ii) have completed peer-review training, and (iii) therefore have at least five years of post-fellowship experience. She has only three. By the contrapositive chain, she does not supervise a first-year resident.
explanations.A: Affirms the consequent. The chain runs from 'supervises' to the training and experience requirements, not the reverse.
explanations.B: Correct.
explanations.C: Two-part claim: the first half (not completed training) follows, but the stimulus says nothing about eligibility to complete the training — it rules out current completion only.
explanations.D: Collapses the restricted conditional into a universal about everyone who has ever supervised a first-year resident in any capacity — the stimulus's rule is stated about endocrinologists currently supervising.
explanations.E: The stimulus gives no distributional claim about endocrinologists generally.

lr.difficultyReason: Requires combining a universal, a most-statement, and a some-statement to derive a guaranteed overlap (some-plus-most chain). Trap (B) is a most-to-all overreach; trap (E) is a could-be-true overlap the statements do not force.
lr.stimulus: Every journal indexed by the Central Linguistics Database requires double-blind peer review of submitted articles. Most journals indexed by the Central Linguistics Database publish at least one issue devoted to fieldwork methodology each year. Some journals that publish an issue devoted to fieldwork methodology each year also publish articles in at least three languages besides English. No journal that requires double-blind peer review accepts advertising from textbook publishers.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following must be true on the basis of the statements above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: At least some journals that publish an issue devoted to fieldwork methodology each year do not accept advertising from textbook publishers.

choices.label: B
choices.text: All journals indexed by the Central Linguistics Database publish at least one issue devoted to fieldwork methodology each year.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Every journal that publishes articles in at least three languages besides English is indexed by the Central Linguistics Database.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Most journals that publish articles in at least three languages besides English do not accept advertising from textbook publishers.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Some journals indexed by the Central Linguistics Database publish articles in at least three languages besides English.

explanations.correct: Most indexed journals publish a fieldwork-methodology issue, which means at least some indexed journals do. Every indexed journal requires double-blind peer review, and no journal that requires that review accepts textbook-publisher advertising. So at least some journals that publish a fieldwork-methodology issue do not accept such advertising.
explanations.A: Correct.
explanations.B: Most-to-all overreach. The stimulus says 'most,' not 'all.'
explanations.C: Converse error. The stimulus tells us what indexed journals do, not that every journal publishing in multiple languages is indexed.
explanations.D: Could be true but not must. The three-languages group is only linked to the methodology-issue group via 'some,' which doesn't support a claim about 'most.'
explanations.E: Could be true but not must. The overlap between 'methodology-issue' journals and 'three-languages' journals is partial; those 'three-languages' journals need not be indexed ones.

lr.difficultyReason: Pigeonhole reasoning over five committee members with overlapping constraints plus a conditional. Traps include a miscounted overlap (C) and an out-of-scope inference (E).
lr.stimulus: The Ferren Arts Council Grant Committee consists of exactly five members. Each member specializes in exactly one of the following four disciplines: theater, dance, visual art, or music. At least one member specializes in each discipline. No theater specialist on the committee also serves on the Ferren Festival Board. Every visual-art specialist on the committee serves on the Ferren Festival Board.
lr.questionStem: If the statements above are true, which one of the following must also be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: At least three members of the committee do not serve on the Ferren Festival Board.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Exactly one member of the committee specializes in each of theater, dance, and music.

choices.label: C
choices.text: More committee members serve on the Ferren Festival Board than do not.

choices.label: D
choices.text: At least one member of the committee serves on the Ferren Festival Board.

choices.label: E
choices.text: No dance specialist on the committee serves on the Ferren Festival Board.

explanations.correct: Each of the four disciplines has at least one specialist, so at least one member is a visual-art specialist. Every visual-art specialist serves on the Festival Board. Therefore, at least one committee member serves on the Festival Board.
explanations.A: Miscounts. With five members and four disciplines each represented, the distribution of non-board members is not fixed — only the theater specialists must not serve on the board, and there is at least one, not necessarily three.
explanations.B: Could be true but not must. One of the four disciplines could have two specialists (with the fifth slot unknown), but the stimulus does not force a particular distribution.
explanations.C: Cannot be determined. The number of members on the board depends on the unspecified distribution across disciplines.
explanations.D: Correct.
explanations.E: Out of scope. The stimulus is silent on whether dance specialists serve on the Festival Board.

lr.difficultyReason: Requires reading 'unless' correctly and chaining it through two further conditionals and a contrapositive applied to a named case. Trap (A) is a converse error; trap (C) overreaches a 'some' to an 'all.'
lr.stimulus: No appellate brief filed in the Fourth Circuit is accepted for oral argument unless it cites at least three prior circuit decisions. Any brief accepted for oral argument in the Fourth Circuit that challenges a statute on constitutional grounds is assigned to a three-judge panel. Every brief assigned to a three-judge panel is subject to expedited scheduling. The Ortiz brief was filed in the Fourth Circuit, challenges a statute on constitutional grounds, and is not subject to expedited scheduling.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following must be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Any brief filed in the Fourth Circuit that cites at least three prior circuit decisions is accepted for oral argument.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Ortiz brief cites fewer than three prior circuit decisions.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Ortiz brief has not been accepted for oral argument.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Every brief filed in the Fourth Circuit that challenges a statute on constitutional grounds is subject to expedited scheduling.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Most briefs filed in the Fourth Circuit are assigned to a three-judge panel.

explanations.correct: If the Ortiz brief had been accepted for oral argument, then because it challenges a statute on constitutional grounds, it would be assigned to a three-judge panel, and hence subject to expedited scheduling. It is not subject to expedited scheduling, so by contrapositive chain it has not been accepted for oral argument.
explanations.A: Converse error. The citation rule is necessary for acceptance, not sufficient.
explanations.B: Could be true but not must. The failure to be subject to expedited scheduling is fully explained by the brief's not being accepted for oral argument; nothing forces a particular citation count.
explanations.C: Correct.
explanations.D: Overreaches. The expedited-scheduling rule kicks in only after a brief is accepted for oral argument.
explanations.E: Unsupported. The stimulus gives no distributional claim about briefs generally.

lr.difficultyReason: Requires chaining two conditionals, applying a contrapositive, and combining the result with a quantifier claim about a named species. Trap (B) is an affirming-the-consequent error; trap (D) is a scope shift.
lr.stimulus: Every amphibian species native to the Caledon Wetlands whose larvae require still water to develop has suffered a population decline of more than 30 percent since the 2005 drainage project. Any Caledon-native amphibian species that has suffered a population decline of more than 30 percent since 2005 has been placed on the provincial watch list. No Caledon-native amphibian species currently approved for commercial harvest is on the provincial watch list. The Caledon mud-frog is a Caledon-native amphibian species whose larvae require still water to develop.
lr.questionStem: If the statements above are true, which one of the following must also be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Caledon mud-frog is not currently approved for commercial harvest.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Any Caledon-native amphibian species on the provincial watch list has larvae that require still water to develop.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Most Caledon-native amphibian species have suffered a population decline of more than 30 percent since 2005.

choices.label: D
choices.text: No amphibian species on the provincial watch list is approved for commercial harvest anywhere in the province.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The Caledon mud-frog's population would not have declined by more than 30 percent if the 2005 drainage project had not occurred.

explanations.correct: The mud-frog's larvae require still water, so it has suffered a 30%+ decline, and so it is on the watch list. No Caledon-native species approved for commercial harvest is on the watch list. Hence the mud-frog is not currently approved for commercial harvest.
explanations.A: Correct.
explanations.B: Affirming the consequent. The conditional runs from 'still water' to 'declined,' not back.
explanations.C: Unsupported. The stimulus constrains only still-water-larvae species, not the broader Caledon amphibian population.
explanations.D: Scope shift. The rule applies to Caledon-native species, not to amphibian species on the watch list from anywhere in the province.
explanations.E: Causal overreach. The stimulus correlates the drainage with declines but does not license a counterfactual claim about what would have happened otherwise.

lr.difficultyReason: Requires combining two universal conditionals with a most-statement and a some-statement to derive a guaranteed existential, then reject an overreach about the same set. Traps include a most-to-all overreach (C) and a scope shift (E).
lr.stimulus: Every sovereign bond issued by a country with an investment-grade credit rating is eligible for purchase by the regional pension fund. Most sovereign bonds eligible for purchase by the regional pension fund carry a maturity of ten years or longer. No sovereign bond that carries a maturity of ten years or longer is included in the fund's short-duration index. Some sovereign bonds issued by countries with an investment-grade credit rating are denominated in currencies other than the euro.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following must be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: At least some sovereign bonds eligible for purchase by the regional pension fund are not included in the fund's short-duration index.

choices.label: B
choices.text: No sovereign bond issued by a country with an investment-grade credit rating is included in the fund's short-duration index.

choices.label: C
choices.text: All sovereign bonds issued by countries with an investment-grade credit rating carry a maturity of ten years or longer.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Most sovereign bonds denominated in currencies other than the euro are eligible for purchase by the regional pension fund.

choices.label: E
choices.text: No short-duration-index bond is denominated in a currency other than the euro.

explanations.correct: Most eligible bonds carry a ten-plus-year maturity, so at least some do. No ten-plus-year bond is in the short-duration index. Hence at least some eligible bonds are not in the short-duration index.
explanations.A: Correct.
explanations.B: Overreach. Only the bonds with ten-plus-year maturity are excluded from the short-duration index — some investment-grade bonds might have shorter maturities.
explanations.C: Most-to-all overreach. The stimulus says 'most eligible,' not 'all investment-grade.'
explanations.D: Reverses the direction of 'some.' The stimulus says some investment-grade bonds are non-euro-denominated, not that most non-euro-denominated bonds are eligible.
explanations.E: Out of scope. The stimulus gives no information about the currency denomination of short-duration-index bonds.

lr.difficultyReason: Requires applying a contrapositive of a conjunctive conditional and chaining it with two further conditionals. Trap (E) is a scope shift; trap (A) converts 'some' into 'most.'
lr.stimulus: If an enterprise software release is distributed to customers without having passed both regression testing and security audit, the release team must file a post-release incident report. No release for which a post-release incident report has been filed is eligible for the quarterly reliability bonus. Every release that fails security audit is rescheduled for the following quarter. Some releases rescheduled for the following quarter are later withdrawn entirely.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following must be true on the basis of the statements above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Most releases that fail security audit are later withdrawn entirely.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Any release that is eligible for the quarterly reliability bonus has passed both regression testing and security audit.

choices.label: C
choices.text: No release distributed without passing security audit is later withdrawn entirely.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Every release that has passed regression testing is eligible for the quarterly reliability bonus.

choices.label: E
choices.text: No release that has been rescheduled for the following quarter is eligible for the quarterly reliability bonus.

explanations.correct: If a release is distributed without passing both tests, an incident report is filed, and no such release is bonus-eligible. By contrapositive, any bonus-eligible release must have been distributed after passing both regression testing and security audit.
explanations.A: Some-to-most overreach. The stimulus says some rescheduled releases are withdrawn, not that most security-audit-failing releases are.
explanations.B: Correct.
explanations.C: Overreach. A release that fails security audit is rescheduled rather than distributed, but the stimulus does not say it can never later be withdrawn — some rescheduled releases are.
explanations.D: Overreaches. Passing regression testing alone doesn't guarantee bonus eligibility; security audit must also be passed, and the stimulus doesn't state regression passage is sufficient.
explanations.E: Scope shift. The stimulus ties bonus ineligibility to incident reports, not directly to rescheduling.

lr.difficultyReason: Requires combining a universal, a some-statement, and a second universal to derive a guaranteed existential, while avoiding a tempting converse trap and a miscounted pigeonhole claim.
lr.stimulus: Every bioethics course offered by the Hargrove Institute this year includes at least one unit on informed consent. Any bioethics course that includes a unit on informed consent also includes a unit on privacy. Some bioethics courses offered by the Hargrove Institute this year are team-taught by a physician and a philosopher. No team-taught bioethics course at the Hargrove Institute has an enrollment cap below 20 students.
lr.questionStem: If the statements above are true, which one of the following must also be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: At least some bioethics courses that include a unit on privacy have an enrollment cap of at least 20 students.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Every bioethics course that includes a unit on privacy is team-taught by a physician and a philosopher.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Most bioethics courses at the Hargrove Institute are team-taught.

choices.label: D
choices.text: No bioethics course at the Hargrove Institute with an enrollment cap below 20 students includes a unit on informed consent.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Some bioethics courses at the Hargrove Institute do not include a unit on informed consent.

explanations.correct: Some Hargrove bioethics courses are team-taught. Every Hargrove bioethics course includes a unit on informed consent, and therefore also on privacy. Team-taught courses have an enrollment cap of at least 20. So at least some courses that include a unit on privacy have an enrollment cap of at least 20.
explanations.A: Correct.
explanations.B: Converse error. Team-teaching is not a necessary condition for including a privacy unit.
explanations.C: Some-to-most overreach.
explanations.D: Contradicted by the stimulus — every Hargrove bioethics course includes informed consent.
explanations.E: Contradicted by the stimulus — every such course includes the unit on informed consent.

lr.difficultyReason: Requires reading a biconditional-style 'only if' and combining it with two further conditionals and a named case. Trap (C) is a converse error; trap (D) is a could-be-true.
lr.stimulus: A municipal ordinance proposed in Westbrook advances to the second reading only if it has been endorsed by at least three members of the Planning Board. Any ordinance endorsed by at least three members of the Planning Board is referred to the City Solicitor for a legal sufficiency review. Every ordinance referred to the City Solicitor for a legal sufficiency review is posted to the public docket. Ordinance 2026-11, proposed in Westbrook, has not been posted to the public docket.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following must be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ordinance 2026-11 has not been endorsed by at least three members of the Planning Board.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ordinance 2026-11 has been rejected by a majority of the Planning Board.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Any Westbrook ordinance posted to the public docket has been endorsed by at least three members of the Planning Board.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Ordinance 2026-11 will be withdrawn before its second reading.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Every Westbrook ordinance that has advanced to the second reading has been posted to the public docket.

explanations.correct: If Ordinance 2026-11 had been endorsed by at least three Planning Board members, it would have been referred for legal sufficiency review, and thus posted to the public docket. It has not been posted. By contrapositive chain, it has not been endorsed by three or more Planning Board members.
explanations.A: Correct.
explanations.B: Overreach. Not being endorsed by at least three members is consistent with being endorsed by one or two, or with no vote yet having been taken.
explanations.C: Converse error. Posting follows from referral, not the other way.
explanations.D: Could be true but not must. The stimulus describes procedural requirements, not future withdrawal.
explanations.E: Overreach. Advancing to second reading requires Planning Board endorsement, but the stimulus does not establish a universal rule that every advanced ordinance has completed the posting step.

lr.difficultyReason: Requires combining two universal conditionals and a 'most' statement to derive a guaranteed existential about a triple overlap, then avoiding a tempting overreach to 'all.' Trap (D) collapses 'most' into 'all'; trap (E) is a scope shift.
lr.stimulus: Every parish church in the Ladon diocese whose foundation predates 1650 is listed in the regional architectural register. Any church listed in the regional architectural register must use lime-based mortar in any restoration work. Most parish churches in the Ladon diocese whose foundation predates 1650 have undergone at least one exterior restoration since 2000. No church that has undergone an exterior restoration since 2000 has had its bell tower demolished.
lr.questionStem: If the statements above are true, which one of the following must also be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: At least some churches that have used lime-based mortar in restoration work have not had their bell towers demolished.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Every church in the regional architectural register has a foundation that predates 1650.

choices.label: C
choices.text: No church with a foundation predating 1650 has had its bell tower demolished.

choices.label: D
choices.text: All parish churches in the Ladon diocese with foundations predating 1650 have undergone at least one exterior restoration since 2000.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Any church in the Ladon diocese that uses lime-based mortar has a foundation predating 1650.

explanations.correct: Most pre-1650 Ladon parish churches have undergone an exterior restoration since 2000, so at least some have. Every pre-1650 such church is on the register, and any church on the register must use lime-based mortar in restoration work. So the restored pre-1650 churches used lime-based mortar. None of those has had its bell tower demolished. Hence at least some churches that used lime-based mortar in restoration have not had their bell towers demolished.
explanations.A: Correct.
explanations.B: Converse error. Being listed in the register does not by itself imply a pre-1650 foundation.
explanations.C: Most-to-all overreach. Only the pre-1650 churches that were restored since 2000 are covered by the no-demolition rule.
explanations.D: Most-to-all overreach.
explanations.E: Converse error. Using lime-based mortar is a requirement imposed on register-listed churches, not a property unique to pre-1650 foundations.

lr.difficultyReason: Two plainly juxtaposed facts — park expansion yet attendance decline — with one obvious confounder (a competing attraction) that explains the decline without contradicting the expansion.
lr.stimulus: Last year, the town of Millbrook doubled the size of Riverside Park and added new playgrounds, picnic areas, and walking trails. Yet annual attendance at Riverside Park fell by nearly 30 percent compared with the previous year.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to resolve the apparent paradox?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Riverside Park's budget for maintenance did not increase along with its size.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A large new amusement park opened five miles from Millbrook last year, drawing many of Riverside Park's former visitors.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The walking trails at Riverside Park are longer than any others in the region.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Millbrook's population has been growing steadily for the past decade.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Attendance at Riverside Park had been rising each year for the five years before the expansion.

explanations.correct: The expansion made the park more appealing, which should have raised attendance; the competing new amusement park siphoned visitors away. Both facts can be true at once once the alternative attraction is introduced.
explanations.A: Lower maintenance relative to size might hurt the park, but nothing in the stimulus suggests visitors noticed neglect — it doesn't explain the sharp drop.
explanations.B: Correct.
explanations.C: Irrelevant — a superlative about the trails doesn't address why fewer people came.
explanations.D: Deepens the paradox — a growing population should have raised, not lowered, attendance at an expanded park.
explanations.E: Deepens the paradox — a rising trend before the expansion makes the post-expansion drop even more surprising.

lr.difficultyReason: Hospital ER: more patients yet shorter waits. The obvious resolution is a large staffing increase that more than kept pace with the patient rise.
lr.stimulus: St. Alban's Hospital reports that the number of patients arriving at its emergency room rose by 25 percent this year over last year. Nonetheless, the average time a patient waited before being seen by a physician fell from 45 minutes to 30 minutes during the same period.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to resolve the apparent paradox?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Most of the hospital's patients this year came from neighborhoods that are farther from the hospital than last year's patients were.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Patients at the hospital have expressed higher satisfaction with their care this year than last year.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The hospital doubled the number of emergency-room physicians and nurses on duty at the start of this year.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The hospital's emergency room is now the only one operating in the county.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Last year's wait times at St. Alban's were longer than wait times at most other hospitals in the region.

explanations.correct: A 25 percent rise in patients should lengthen waits, but doubling the clinical staff dramatically increases throughput — enough to absorb the added demand and shorten waits overall.
explanations.A: Travel distance affects arrival, not in-hospital wait time after arrival.
explanations.B: Patient satisfaction is a consequence, not an explanation, of shorter waits.
explanations.C: Correct.
explanations.D: Deepens the paradox — being the only ER in the county would concentrate demand and lengthen waits.
explanations.E: Comparison with other hospitals doesn't explain St. Alban's own year-over-year change.

lr.difficultyReason: Local habitat destroyed yet species population rises — resolved by the single obvious fact that the birds relocated to a protected site.
lr.stimulus: Biologists report that more than half of the marshland surrounding Lake Corren, the traditional nesting site of the yellow-throated tern, was drained for farmland during the past five years. Despite this, the regional population of yellow-throated terns increased by 15 percent over the same period.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to resolve the apparent paradox?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The yellow-throated tern eats primarily small fish that are abundant in Lake Corren.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Farmland drained from marshes is usually less productive than farmland that was never marshland.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Five years ago a large, previously unknown wetland 20 miles from Lake Corren was designated a protected bird sanctuary, and most of the displaced terns nested there successfully.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The yellow-throated tern is closely related to several other tern species whose populations have declined.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Drainage of the marshland around Lake Corren has been more extensive than biologists initially predicted.

explanations.correct: The new protected wetland gave the displaced terns somewhere to go. Habitat was lost at Lake Corren, but equivalent habitat became available nearby — so regional numbers could still rise.
explanations.A: Food availability at the old site doesn't explain how the population grew after half that site was destroyed.
explanations.B: A fact about the farmland, not the terns — doesn't address the population figure.
explanations.C: Correct.
explanations.D: Irrelevant — the paradox is about this species, not its relatives.
explanations.E: Deepens the paradox — more drainage should have harmed the population further.

lr.difficultyReason: Fewer downloads yet higher revenue — resolved by a shift to higher-priced enterprise licenses. Single clear mechanism.
lr.stimulus: Vortex Software reports that the total number of downloads of its flagship design program fell by 20 percent last year compared with the year before. Even so, Vortex's revenue from that program rose by 35 percent over the same period.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to resolve the apparent paradox?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Last year Vortex began offering the program primarily to corporate customers through licenses that cost many times more than a single-user download.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Vortex's main competitor released a similar program last year at a lower price.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Most of Vortex's downloads last year came from first-time users rather than from returning customers.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Vortex's advertising budget was smaller last year than in the year before.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Vortex's development costs for the program were higher last year than the year before.

explanations.correct: If each corporate license brings in many times what a single download does, a smaller number of high-value licenses can easily yield 35 percent more revenue than a larger number of low-value downloads.
explanations.A: Correct.
explanations.B: Deepens the paradox — a cheaper competitor should have depressed Vortex's revenue, not raised it.
explanations.C: First-time versus returning users doesn't explain the revenue rise.
explanations.D: Smaller ad spend might explain fewer downloads but not higher revenue.
explanations.E: Costs don't determine revenue — this doesn't address the question.

lr.difficultyReason: Museum attendance rises while gift-shop revenue falls — resolved by noting the new visitors came on free-admission days when spending is far lower.
lr.stimulus: The Hartwell Museum of History reports that total annual visitors rose by 40 percent after it introduced a new free-admission day each month last year. However, revenue from the museum's gift shop fell by 10 percent during the same period.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to resolve the apparent paradox?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Nearly all of the museum's increased attendance came on the new free-admission days, and visitors on those days spend, on average, far less in the gift shop than paying visitors do.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The gift shop at the museum offers a wider variety of items than any comparable museum shop in the city.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Most items in the museum's gift shop are priced higher than comparable items elsewhere.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Attendance at other history museums in the region rose last year as well.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The museum's overall operating budget was lower last year than the year before.

explanations.correct: If the extra visitors overwhelmingly came on free days and spend very little, then gift-shop revenue can fall even as attendance rises — the new crowd simply isn't buying.
explanations.A: Correct.
explanations.B: A fact about product variety doesn't explain a revenue decline.
explanations.C: Higher prices could raise revenue per sale or deter sales — ambiguous, and it doesn't tie to the attendance surge.
explanations.D: Irrelevant — other museums' numbers don't explain Hartwell's shop revenue.
explanations.E: The budget doesn't determine how much visitors spend in the gift shop.

lr.difficultyReason: Concert attendance up but ticket revenue down — one-step resolution via a deep ticket discount.
lr.stimulus: The Bayside Symphony reports that attendance at its concerts rose by 50 percent this season over last season. Nevertheless, total ticket revenue for the season fell by 20 percent.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to resolve the apparent paradox?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The symphony performed the same number of concerts this season as last season.

choices.label: B
choices.text: This season the symphony cut the price of every ticket by more than half in order to fill empty seats.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Attendance at competing orchestras in the region also rose this season.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The symphony's musicians received a modest pay raise at the start of this season.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Reviews of this season's performances were on the whole more positive than last season's.

explanations.correct: Cutting every ticket's price by more than half while attendance rises only 50 percent means revenue per seat drops faster than seats sold rise. Total revenue can fall even as audiences grow.
explanations.A: Holding the number of concerts constant rules out one alternative explanation but doesn't itself explain lower revenue.
explanations.B: Correct.
explanations.C: Other orchestras' attendance is irrelevant to Bayside's revenue.
explanations.D: Musician pay is a cost, not a revenue figure.
explanations.E: Better reviews would tend to raise ticket demand and revenue, if anything.

lr.difficultyReason: Lower speed limit yet more fatalities — resolved by a sharp rise in traffic volume that overwhelms the per-driver safety gain.
lr.stimulus: Three years ago, the state of Corinth lowered the speed limit on its rural highways from 65 to 55 miles per hour, expecting a reduction in traffic fatalities. Yet the total number of traffic fatalities on those highways has risen by 12 percent since the change took effect.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to resolve the apparent paradox?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Drivers in Corinth have reported feeling safer on the highways since the speed-limit change.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Some neighboring states have retained higher speed limits on their rural highways.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Since the speed-limit change, the total number of vehicles using Corinth's rural highways has more than doubled.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Police in Corinth have issued more speeding tickets each year since the change than they did before.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Most fatal accidents on rural highways involve drivers who were unfamiliar with the route.

explanations.correct: Fatalities depend on both the per-mile risk and the number of miles driven. Doubling the traffic can produce more total deaths even when each trip is safer — so both facts can be true.
explanations.A: Feelings of safety don't bear on the actual fatality count.
explanations.B: Neighboring states' rules don't explain Corinth's own change.
explanations.C: Correct.
explanations.D: More tickets suggests more speeding, which would deepen rather than resolve the paradox about a lower limit.
explanations.E: A general fact about fatal accidents doesn't explain why the count rose after the limit dropped.

lr.difficultyReason: Printed-dictionary sales fall while word-lookup volume rises — resolved by noting lookups migrated to free online dictionaries.
lr.stimulus: Sales of printed English dictionaries in the country of Lindoria have fallen by more than 60 percent over the past decade. However, surveys indicate that the total number of times Lindorians looked up the meaning of an English word rose substantially during that same decade.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to resolve the apparent paradox?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Most printed dictionaries sold in Lindoria are purchased as gifts rather than for personal use.

choices.label: B
choices.text: During the past decade, free online dictionaries have become widely available in Lindoria, and most word lookups there now take place on those sites.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Lindorian schools have begun assigning fewer writing exercises than they did a decade ago.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Printed dictionaries now cost considerably more than they did ten years ago.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The average English vocabulary of an adult Lindorian has grown modestly over the past decade.

explanations.correct: If lookups simply moved from printed books to free online sites, Lindorians can look up more words overall while buying far fewer printed dictionaries. Both halves of the paradox are explained at once.
explanations.A: Gift-versus-personal use is orthogonal to whether lookups are happening elsewhere.
explanations.B: Correct.
explanations.C: Fewer writing exercises would tend to lower lookups, deepening the paradox.
explanations.D: Higher prices help explain the sales drop alone but not why lookups rose.
explanations.E: A modest vocabulary rise doesn't by itself account for more lookups with fewer dictionaries.

lr.difficultyReason: Fewer arrests yet more convictions — resolved by noting prosecutors now pursue only cases with stronger evidence, raising the conviction rate enough to offset fewer arrests.
lr.stimulus: The Oakridge County district attorney reports that the number of arrests for burglary in the county fell by 30 percent last year compared with the year before. Even so, the number of burglary convictions obtained in the county's courts rose by 15 percent during the same period.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to resolve the apparent paradox?

choices.label: A
choices.text: At the start of last year the district attorney's office adopted a policy of taking only burglary cases supported by strong physical evidence to trial, and the share of such cases ending in conviction has risen sharply.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Oakridge County has the highest burglary rate of any county in the state.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Many of those arrested for burglary in previous years were repeat offenders.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Last year judges in Oakridge County imposed longer sentences for burglary than in any recent year.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Defense attorneys in Oakridge County are widely regarded as among the most effective in the state.

explanations.correct: When only strong-evidence cases go to trial, a much higher share convict. Even with fewer arrests feeding the pipeline, that higher conviction share can yield more total convictions.
explanations.A: Correct.
explanations.B: A baseline rate doesn't explain a year-over-year change.
explanations.C: Repeat-offender status is a background fact; it doesn't address why convictions rose.
explanations.D: Sentence length is about punishment, not whether convictions occur.
explanations.E: Strong defense attorneys would tend to lower, not raise, conviction counts — deepening the paradox.

lr.difficultyReason: Ethicists publicly endorse a principle yet privately decline to follow it — resolved by a single clear distinction between the principle they endorse and the one the situation would require.
lr.stimulus: In a recent survey, 90 percent of professional ethicists publicly endorsed the principle that people have a strong duty to give substantial portions of their income to charity. Yet when asked about their own practice, nearly all of those same ethicists reported giving only a very small share of their income to charity.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to resolve the apparent paradox?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Most of the ethicists surveyed work at universities where salaries are lower than those in comparable professions.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The principle that most of the ethicists endorsed applies, by its own terms, only to people whose income is many times higher than any of the surveyed ethicists earn.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Charities in the ethicists' communities have received less total funding this year than last year.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Ethicists surveyed in previous years endorsed the same principle at a similar rate.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Most people who donate to charity give without first consulting any ethical principle.

explanations.correct: If the endorsed principle by its own terms applies only to much higher earners, the ethicists' low giving is consistent with their endorsement — the duty they accept simply doesn't bind people at their income level.
explanations.A: Lower salaries might explain small gifts but not why the ethicists endorse a demanding duty they appear to ignore.
explanations.B: Correct.
explanations.C: Community-wide funding totals don't address the ethicists' individual giving.
explanations.D: Historical endorsement rates don't reconcile the gap between words and deeds.
explanations.E: A claim about most donors doesn't speak to ethicists, who are defined by engaging with principles.

lr.difficultyReason: Vaccination coverage rose while the proportion of hospitalized flu patients who were vaccinated also rose — a genuine tension that dissolves only once one recognizes the base-rate shift: when nearly everyone is vaccinated, most of the unavoidable residual cases will by arithmetic be among vaccinated people. The trap answers each explain the rise in coverage or the rise in hospitalizations in isolation.
lr.stimulus: Public-health officials report that the share of adults in Kerrow Province who received the annual flu vaccine rose from 40 percent to 85 percent over the past decade. Nevertheless, the proportion of patients hospitalized for influenza during that period who had been vaccinated also rose sharply — from 18 percent to 70 percent.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to resolve the apparent discrepancy in the information above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The influenza vaccine substantially reduces, but does not eliminate, a vaccinated person's risk of contracting the flu.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Hospitals in Kerrow Province have expanded their capacity to treat influenza patients over the past decade.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Public-health officials in Kerrow Province encouraged older adults, who are more likely to be hospitalized if infected, to receive the vaccine.

choices.label: D
choices.text: New strains of influenza circulating in the past decade have been more virulent than those circulating earlier.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Patients who are vaccinated against influenza typically recover from hospitalization more quickly than unvaccinated patients do.

explanations.correct: When 85 percent of adults are vaccinated, the unvaccinated pool is tiny; any residual hospitalizations are drawn mostly from the vaccinated majority even though each vaccinated person is individually at lower risk. Both facts coexist once one sees that a large vaccinated share produces a large vaccinated share of cases by sheer base rate.
explanations.A: Correct.
explanations.B: Expanded hospital capacity doesn't explain the composition of the hospitalized population by vaccination status.
explanations.C: Deepens the paradox — if the people most likely to be hospitalized were prioritized for vaccination, one would expect vaccination to reduce their share of hospitalizations.
explanations.D: Would explain a rise in hospitalizations overall but does not explain why the vaccinated share of them rose so sharply.
explanations.E: Recovery time doesn't bear on the proportion of hospitalized patients who had been vaccinated.

lr.difficultyReason: Raising the minimum wage should, on the standard story, reduce employment in low-wage sectors; yet employment rose. Resolution requires noticing a confounder — the low-wage sector expanded because consumers had more money to spend. Traps explain only half the picture or invoke the wrong mechanism.
lr.stimulus: Two years ago, the state of Velmar raised its minimum wage by 35 percent. Economists had predicted that employment in low-wage sectors such as food service and retail would fall. However, employment in those sectors has since risen by 8 percent, even as the predicted wage floor was strictly enforced.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to resolve the apparent discrepancy in the information above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Most low-wage workers in Velmar spend nearly all their additional earnings on goods and services provided by the food-service and retail sectors, increasing demand for those sectors' workers.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Inflation in Velmar has outpaced that of neighboring states over the past two years.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The minimum wage in Velmar is now higher than that of any neighboring state.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Some low-wage employers in Velmar have responded to the increase by reducing their employees' weekly hours.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Before the wage increase, food-service and retail businesses in Velmar had unusually high rates of employee turnover.

explanations.correct: The predicted drop assumed demand for low-wage labor would be roughly fixed. If raising wages routes money right back into the sectors that employ those workers, demand for their labor actually grows, absorbing the higher wage cost and producing net hiring. Both the wage increase and the employment rise are explained by a single mechanism.
explanations.A: Correct.
explanations.B: Higher inflation might erode the real value of the wage increase but doesn't explain why employment rose.
explanations.C: A cross-state comparison doesn't explain within-Velmar employment changes.
explanations.D: Deepens the paradox in a sense — hour reductions would point toward employers cutting back on labor, the opposite of what was observed.
explanations.E: Prior turnover rates don't explain why employment levels rose after the wage increase.

lr.difficultyReason: Pesticide use fell dramatically yet pollinator populations continued to decline — a tension that resolves once a second environmental factor (habitat loss from agricultural expansion driven by the same policy) is introduced. Distractors cite unrelated environmental stressors or re-describe the decline.
lr.stimulus: Over the past decade, farmers in the Landry River basin, following a widely adopted voluntary program, reduced their use of bee-toxic pesticides by nearly two-thirds. Yet during the same period, populations of native bees and other pollinators in the basin continued to decline at roughly the same rate as before the program began.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to resolve the apparent discrepancy in the information above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Other regions that did not adopt the voluntary pesticide-reduction program have also seen pollinator populations decline, though at a slower rate.

choices.label: B
choices.text: To offset lower yields from reduced pesticide use, farmers in the Landry basin cleared large tracts of hedgerow and wildflower meadow to plant additional crop acreage.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Many of the pesticides that remained in use after the reductions are still moderately harmful to pollinators.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Some farmers in the Landry basin adopted the voluntary program only in its final years.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Pollinator populations are difficult to count accurately because the insects range widely across agricultural landscapes.

explanations.correct: If the very program that reduced pesticide exposure also drove farmers to destroy the wild habitats pollinators depend on, the lost habitat offsets the chemical benefit. Both facts — reduced pesticide use and continued decline — become mutually consistent once the habitat-loss channel is made visible.
explanations.A: A slower decline elsewhere actually suggests the program helped a little, but doesn't explain why the program's basin continued to decline at the prior rate.
explanations.B: Correct.
explanations.C: Residual harm would slow the expected gains, not eliminate them — and wouldn't explain continued decline at the prior rate.
explanations.D: Late adoption might delay benefits for some farms but can't account for a basin-wide two-thirds reduction producing no effect.
explanations.E: Measurement difficulty calls the data into question rather than explaining it.

lr.difficultyReason: More automated tests yet more bugs in production — resolved by a measurement artifact: the automated tests surface bugs that were previously shipping undetected, so 'bugs found' grew even as shipped-bug quality rose. Trap answers invoke the wrong direction of causation or target the wrong metric.
lr.stimulus: At Horizon Software, the engineering team doubled its investment in automated testing over the past year, and the number of tests run before each release more than tripled. Even so, the number of bugs reported by users within 30 days of each release rose by 20 percent over the same year.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to resolve the apparent discrepancy in the information above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Most of Horizon's engineers have been writing automated tests for less than two years.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Horizon's main competitors have also reported rising user bug counts over the past year.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The expansion of automated testing allowed Horizon to confidently ship four times as many new features as it did the previous year.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Some categories of bugs can be caught only through manual testing, which Horizon reduced as automation expanded.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Users have become more likely to file bug reports than they were a year ago.

explanations.correct: If automated testing let Horizon ship four times as many features, each feature carrying even a modest bug rate would yield many more total bugs overall. Automated tests can raise per-feature reliability while the sheer volume of shipped features increases bug totals. Both facts are then jointly true.
explanations.A: If anything, this weakens automated testing's value but doesn't explain how a tripling of tests still let more bugs through — unless paired with some offsetting factor the answer doesn't supply.
explanations.B: Industry-wide trends don't explain Horizon's specific year-over-year change.
explanations.C: Correct.
explanations.D: Provides a plausible partial mechanism — reduced manual testing could leak bugs — but doesn't explain why the team's overall testing program, which tripled total tests, failed to prevent a net rise; it is too narrow and depends on an undisclosed tradeoff.
explanations.E: A reporting-propensity change would explain the rise in reports without assuming any real change in bugs, but it doesn't connect to the expansion in automated testing that is the other half of the tension.

lr.difficultyReason: Average reading scores fell despite curriculum improvements — resolved by a selection-effect shift in which students were tested. Distractors invoke plausible but orthogonal causes.
lr.stimulus: The Brookford school district overhauled its elementary reading curriculum three years ago, incorporating methods that independent studies have shown to improve reading proficiency. Yet the average reading scores of Brookford fifth-graders on the statewide assessment have fallen each year since the new curriculum was introduced.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to resolve the apparent discrepancy in the information above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The statewide assessment is administered each spring by independent proctors, not by Brookford teachers.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Since the new curriculum was introduced, Brookford schools have stopped exempting struggling readers from the assessment, whereas previously such students were routinely excused.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Several neighboring districts have since adopted the same reading curriculum that Brookford adopted.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The statewide assessment was redesigned seven years ago to emphasize inferential reasoning over decoding skills.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Brookford teachers received training in the new curriculum only during the summer before it was introduced.

explanations.correct: If the pool of test-takers now includes students who used to be excused, the tested population is weaker on average even though each individual student may be improving. The curriculum can be working while the average score falls because the measured sample has shifted.
explanations.A: Independent proctoring was presumably also in place before and so doesn't distinguish the before-and-after periods.
explanations.B: Correct.
explanations.C: Neighboring districts' choices don't bear on Brookford's year-over-year scores.
explanations.D: An assessment change seven years ago predates the curriculum overhaul and so can't explain the trend beginning three years ago.
explanations.E: Limited training might blunt the curriculum's impact but wouldn't produce falling scores beyond the baseline — and doesn't reconcile improved methods with worsening results.

lr.difficultyReason: Reported burglaries fell while actual burglaries may not have — a reporting artifact that reconciles falling stats with unchanged or rising victimization. Distractors attribute the drop to policing or target neighboring jurisdictions.
lr.stimulus: According to statistics released by the Haldin Police Department, the number of residential burglaries reported in Haldin fell by 22 percent last year. Nonetheless, an anonymous survey of Haldin residents conducted by an independent research institute found that the proportion of households that had experienced a break-in during the same year was essentially unchanged from the previous year.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to resolve the apparent discrepancy in the information above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Last year, many Haldin insurers began requiring that policyholders file a police report within 24 hours of a burglary to remain eligible for reimbursement.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Last year, several Haldin residents announced they would stop filing police reports after a widely publicized case in which officers were slow to respond to burglary calls.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Haldin Police Department last year reassigned a significant number of officers from burglary investigation to traffic enforcement.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Neighboring cities have reported modest increases in residential burglary over the past year.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Most Haldin burglaries involve the theft of items valued at less than one thousand dollars.

explanations.correct: If a public loss of confidence caused fewer victims to file reports, the official count falls while the underlying rate of break-ins — captured by the anonymous survey — stays the same. Both datasets can be accurate: one measures reporting, the other measures incidence.
explanations.A: Deepens the paradox — tying insurance reimbursement to reports would increase reporting rates, which should raise, not lower, the official count.
explanations.B: Correct.
explanations.C: Reduced investigation resources don't explain a drop in reports filed; victims file regardless of what investigators do afterward.
explanations.D: Cross-city trends don't reconcile the within-Haldin discrepancy.
explanations.E: The value of stolen items is irrelevant to whether burglaries are reported or occurring.

lr.difficultyReason: Surgeons with higher complication rates publish better outcomes — resolved by a selection effect: top surgeons take the hardest cases. Distractors invoke unrelated factors about training or publication practices.
