explanations.correct: Asano is in Cardiology. Bello (Cardiology) and Choi (Dermatology) are in different departments. Diaz and Ellis are both in ER. Choi is not in ER; Fadel is not in ER. Fadel is in Dermatology, not Cardiology, so the Fadel-Cardiology conditional is vacuous. Gur is in Cardiology, not Dermatology, so the Gur-Dermatology conditional is vacuous. Imura is in ER, not Cardiology, so the Imura-Cardiology conditional is vacuous. Exactly one of {Bello (Cardiology), Huang (Dermatology), Imura (ER)} — Huang — is in Dermatology. Every department has exactly three interns.

explanations.B: Bello and Choi are both in Dermatology. Violates the rule that Bello and Choi are in different departments.
explanations.C: Diaz is in Cardiology and Ellis is in ER. Violates the rule that Diaz and Ellis are in the same department.

Testing the remaining distribution and Bello/Choi being split, every valid assignment places Diaz and Ellis together in Dermatology (because ER already holds Gur plus at most two non-Bello/Huang/Imura slots, and Cardiology needs Choi to accompany Fadel so that Bello is free to be in Dermatology or ER without violating the exactly-one rule). Verification across the three satisfying assignments confirms Diaz is in Dermatology in every case.

In every satisfying assignment, Huang is in Cardiology.
explanations.A: Bello is in Dermatology or ER.
explanations.B: Choi is in Cardiology in every valid case.
explanations.C: Correct.
explanations.D: Imura could be in Dermatology or ER.

explanations.B: Choi is in Dermatology in every valid case.

lg.scenario: A farmers-market vendor will arrange exactly nine produce items — apples, basil, carrots, dill, eggplant, fennel, garlic, herbs, and jicama — among three stalls: Front, Middle, and Rear. Each stall contains exactly three items. The arrangement must satisfy the following conditions. Apples are placed in the Front stall. Basil is not placed in the Rear stall. Basil and carrots are placed in different stalls. Dill and fennel are placed in the same stall. If dill is placed in the Front stall, then eggplant is placed in the Middle stall. If fennel is placed in the Rear stall, then garlic is placed in the Front stall. If carrots are placed in the Middle stall, then herbs are placed in the Front stall. Exactly two of herbs, jicama, and eggplant are placed in the Rear stall.

questions.questionStem: Which one of the following could be a complete and accurate arrangement of produce items among the stalls?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Front: apples, basil, herbs; Middle: dill, fennel, garlic; Rear: carrots, eggplant, jicama

choices.label: B
choices.text: Front: basil, garlic, herbs; Middle: apples, dill, fennel; Rear: carrots, eggplant, jicama

choices.label: C
choices.text: Front: apples, basil, carrots; Middle: dill, fennel, herbs; Rear: eggplant, garlic, jicama

choices.label: D
choices.text: Front: apples, basil, fennel; Middle: dill, garlic, herbs; Rear: carrots, eggplant, jicama

choices.label: E
choices.text: Front: apples, basil, jicama; Middle: dill, fennel, herbs; Rear: carrots, eggplant, garlic

explanations.correct: Apples are in Front. Basil (Front) is not in Rear. Basil (Front) and carrots (Rear) are in different stalls. Dill and fennel are both in Middle. Dill is in Middle, not Front, so the dill-Front conditional is vacuous. Fennel is in Middle, not Rear, so the fennel-Rear conditional is vacuous. Carrots are in Rear, not Middle, so the carrots-Middle conditional is vacuous. Of {herbs (Front), jicama (Rear), eggplant (Rear)}, exactly two are in Rear. Each stall has exactly three items.
explanations.A: Correct.
explanations.B: Apples are in Middle, violating the rule that apples are in Front.
explanations.C: Basil and carrots are both in Front, violating the rule that basil and carrots are in different stalls.
explanations.D: Dill is in Middle and fennel is in Front, violating the rule that dill and fennel are in the same stall.
explanations.E: Only eggplant among {herbs, jicama, eggplant} is in Rear, violating the rule that exactly two of these three items are in Rear.

questions.questionStem: If carrots are placed in the Middle stall, then which one of the following must be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Basil is placed in the Middle stall.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Dill is placed in the Front stall.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Eggplant is placed in the Rear stall.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Garlic is placed in the Middle stall.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Jicama is placed in the Middle stall.

explanations.correct: If carrots are in Middle, then herbs are in Front (by the carrots-Middle conditional). Basil must be in Front (basil is not in Rear and must differ from carrots, who are in Middle). Apples are in Front, basil is in Front, herbs are in Front — Front is full. Dill and fennel must be in the same stall; since Front is full, they are both in Middle or both in Rear. If dill and fennel are in Rear, then fennel in Rear forces garlic into Front (but Front is full) — contradiction. So dill and fennel are in Middle, joining carrots — Middle is full. That forces eggplant, jicama, and garlic into Rear. Exactly two of {herbs (Front), jicama (Rear), eggplant (Rear)} are in Rear ✓. So eggplant must be in Rear.
explanations.A: Basil must be in Front.
explanations.B: Dill must be in Middle.
explanations.C: Correct.
explanations.D: Garlic must be in Rear.
explanations.E: Jicama must be in Rear.

questions.questionStem: If jicama is placed in the Front stall, then which one of the following must be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Basil is placed in the Front stall.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Carrots are placed in the Rear stall.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Dill is placed in the Middle stall.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Garlic is placed in the Front stall.

choices.label: E

explanations.correct: If jicama is in Front, then among {herbs, jicama, eggplant} only herbs and eggplant can fill the required two Rear slots. So herbs and eggplant are both in Rear. Dill and fennel are in the same stall. If dill and fennel are in Front, then dill-Front forces eggplant into Middle, contradicting eggplant in Rear. So dill and fennel are both in Middle (they can't both fit in Rear alongside herbs and eggplant). Therefore dill is in Middle.
explanations.A: Basil could be in Front or Middle.
explanations.B: Carrots could be in different stalls (verification shows carrots in Front or Rear among satisfying cases).
explanations.C: Correct.
explanations.D: Garlic could be in Front, Middle, or Rear.
explanations.E: Herbs must be in Rear, not Middle.

questions.questionStem: If herbs are placed in the Front stall, then which one of the following must be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Basil is placed in the Middle stall.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Dill is placed in the Middle stall.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Eggplant is placed in the Middle stall.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Garlic is placed in the Middle stall.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Jicama is placed in the Front stall.

explanations.correct: Exactly two of {herbs, jicama, eggplant} must be in Rear. If herbs are in Front, then both jicama and eggplant must be in Rear. Dill and fennel must be in the same stall; if dill is in Front, then eggplant must be in Middle (contradicting eggplant in Rear). If dill and fennel are in Rear, then fennel in Rear forces garlic into Front, and dill-Rear + fennel-Rear + (jicama or eggplant)-Rear already puts at least three items in Rear, leaving no room. So dill and fennel must both be in Middle.
explanations.A: Basil could be in Front or Middle.
explanations.B: Correct.
explanations.C: Eggplant must be in Rear.
explanations.D: Garlic could be in Front, Middle, or Rear.
explanations.E: Jicama must be in Rear.

questions.questionStem: Each of the following could be true EXCEPT:

choices.label: A
choices.text: Basil is placed in the Middle stall.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Carrots are placed in the Front stall.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Eggplant is placed in the Middle stall.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Fennel is placed in the Rear stall.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Herbs are placed in the Middle stall.

explanations.correct: Suppose fennel is in Rear. Then dill is in Rear (same stall), and garlic must be in Front (by the fennel-Rear conditional). Exactly two of {herbs, jicama, eggplant} must be in Rear — but Rear already holds dill and fennel, plus at least one of {herbs, jicama, eggplant}, for a total of at least three. Adding a second of {herbs, jicama, eggplant} to Rear would make four. Rear can hold only three items total, so at most one of {herbs, jicama, eggplant} can be in Rear — contradicting the exactly-two rule. Therefore fennel cannot be in Rear.
explanations.A: Possible — e.g., Front: apples, carrots, eggplant; Middle: basil, dill, fennel; Rear: garlic, herbs, jicama.
explanations.B: Possible — e.g., Front: apples, carrots, eggplant; Middle: basil, dill, fennel; Rear: garlic, herbs, jicama.
explanations.C: Possible — e.g., Front: apples, basil, garlic; Middle: dill, eggplant, fennel; Rear: carrots, herbs, jicama.
explanations.D: Correct — cannot be true.
explanations.E: Possible — e.g., Front: apples, basil, garlic; Middle: dill, fennel, herbs; Rear: carrots, eggplant, jicama.

lg.scenario: Exactly nine relay runners — Ames, Brio, Cruz, Dao, Eng, Fox, Gill, Han, and Ivy — will be assigned to exactly one of three teams: Red, Blue, and Green. Each team is assigned exactly three runners. The assignment must satisfy the following conditions. Cruz is on the Red team. Ivy is not on the Red team. Ames and Brio are on the same team. Dao and Eng are on different teams. If Fox is on the Blue team, then Gill is on the Green team. If Han is on the Red team, then Ivy is on the Blue team. If Eng is on the Green team, then Ames is on the Red team. Exactly one of Dao, Fox, and Han is on the Red team.

questions.questionStem: Which one of the following could be a complete and accurate assignment of runners to teams?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Red: Cruz, Dao, Gill; Blue: Ames, Brio, Eng; Green: Fox, Han, Ivy

choices.label: B
choices.text: Red: Ames, Brio, Dao; Blue: Cruz, Eng, Fox; Green: Gill, Han, Ivy

choices.text: Red: Cruz, Dao, Gill; Blue: Eng, Fox, Han; Green: Ames, Brio, Ivy

choices.label: E
choices.text: Red: Cruz, Dao, Fox; Blue: Ames, Brio, Eng; Green: Gill, Han, Ivy

explanations.correct: Cruz is on Red. Ivy (Green) is not on Red. Ames and Brio are both on Blue. Dao (Red) and Eng (Blue) are on different teams. Fox is on Green, not Blue, so the Fox-Blue conditional is vacuous. Han is on Green, not Red, so the Han-Red conditional is vacuous. Eng is on Blue, not Green, so the Eng-Green conditional is vacuous. Of {Dao (Red), Fox (Green), Han (Green)}, exactly one — Dao — is on Red. Each team has exactly three runners.
explanations.A: Correct.
explanations.B: Cruz is on Blue, violating the rule that Cruz is on Red.
explanations.C: Ames is on Red and Brio is on Blue, violating the rule that Ames and Brio are on the same team.
explanations.D: Fox is on Blue but Gill is on Red, violating the rule that if Fox is on Blue then Gill is on Green.
explanations.E: Both Dao and Fox are on Red, violating the rule that exactly one of Dao, Fox, and Han is on Red.

questions.questionStem: If Han is on the Red team, then which one of the following must be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ames is on the Blue team.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Dao is on the Blue team.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Eng is on the Red team.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Fox is on the Green team.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Gill is on the Blue team.

explanations.correct: If Han is on Red, then Ivy is on Blue (by the Han-Red conditional). Exactly one of {Dao, Fox, Han} is on Red — since Han occupies that slot, Dao and Fox are not on Red. Dao and Eng are on different teams; if Eng were on Green, Ames would have to be on Red (by the Eng-Green conditional), but then Ames and Brio would both be on Red, joined by Cruz and Han — four on Red, too many. So Eng is not on Green. Eng is not on Blue either in this scenario (Blue already has Ivy and Ames/Brio would have to land somewhere consistent) — running the cases, Eng must be on Red to complete Red (Cruz, Han, Eng). Therefore Eng is on the Red team.
explanations.A: Ames could be on Blue or Green.
explanations.B: Dao could be on Blue or Green.
explanations.C: Correct.
explanations.D: Fox could be on Blue or Green.
explanations.E: Gill could be on Red, Blue, or Green.

questions.questionStem: If Dao is on the Red team, then which one of the following must be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ames is on the Blue team.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Fox is on the Blue team.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Gill is on the Red team.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Han is on the Blue team.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Ivy is on the Blue team.

explanations.correct: If Dao is on Red, then by the exactly-one rule Fox and Han are not on Red. Dao and Eng are on different teams; if Eng were on Green the Eng-Green conditional would force Ames onto Red and therefore Brio onto Red, making Red hold four runners (Cruz, Dao, Ames, Brio) — impossible. So Eng is on Blue. Since Red already holds Cruz and Dao and Fox/Han can't fill the third Red slot, one other runner must be on Red. Eng is on Blue, Ames/Brio are together (so can't split to fill the slot alone), and Ivy can't be on Red — leaving Gill as the only option. Therefore Gill is on the Red team in every valid assignment.
explanations.A: Ames could be on Blue or Green (depending on whether Ames/Brio land on Blue or Green).
explanations.B: Fox cannot be on Blue — Fox is on Green in every valid assignment here.
explanations.C: Correct.
explanations.D: Han could be on Blue or Green.
explanations.E: Ivy could be on Blue or Green.

choices.text: Eng is on the Red team.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Gill is on the Red team.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Han is on the Green team.

explanations.correct: If Fox is on Blue, then Gill is on Green (by the Fox-Blue conditional). Exactly one of {Dao, Fox, Han} is on Red — since Fox is on Blue, either Dao or Han is on Red. If Han is on Red, Ivy is on Blue (by the Han-Red conditional); Dao is not on Red. Dao and Eng are on different teams. Running the deductions, this scenario produces exactly one valid assignment in which Eng ends up on Red together with Cruz and Han. Therefore Eng is on the Red team.
explanations.A: Ames is on Green in the unique satisfying assignment.
explanations.B: Dao is on Blue in the unique satisfying assignment.
explanations.C: Correct.
explanations.D: Gill is on Green, not Red.
explanations.E: Han is on Red, not Green.

questions.questionStem: Each of the following could be true EXCEPT:

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ames is on the Green team.

choices.text: Ivy is on the Green team.

Red already contains Cruz, so Red would hold Cruz, Ames, Brio — that's three, which is fine for group size. But then exactly one of {Dao, Fox, Han} must also be on Red, bringing Red to four. Contradiction — Red can hold only three runners. Therefore Eng cannot be on Green.
explanations.A: Possible — e.g., Red: Cruz, Fox, Eng; Blue: Dao, Gill, Ivy; Green: Ames, Brio, Han.
explanations.B: Possible — e.g., Red: Cruz, Dao, Gill; Blue: Ames, Brio, Eng; Green: Fox, Han, Ivy.
explanations.C: Correct — cannot be true.
explanations.D: Possible — e.g., Red: Cruz, Fox, Eng; Blue: Ames, Brio, Gill; Green: Dao, Han, Ivy.
explanations.E: Possible — e.g., Red: Cruz, Dao, Gill; Blue: Ames, Brio, Eng; Green: Fox, Han, Ivy.

lg.scenario: At a small track meet, exactly five runners — Park, Quinn, Ruiz, Singh, and Tate — will be divided between two relay teams, Blue and Gold. The Blue team has exactly two runners (running leg 1 then leg 2), and the Gold team has exactly three runners (running leg 1, leg 2, then leg 3). The five roster slots are therefore Blue-leg-1, Blue-leg-2, Gold-leg-1, Gold-leg-2, and Gold-leg-3, read as a single early-to-late sequence. Each runner fills exactly one slot. The assignment is subject to the following conditions. Park runs for Blue. Tate runs for Gold. Quinn runs an earlier leg than Ruiz.

explanations.C: Quinn can be at Blue-leg-1, Blue-leg-2, Gold-leg-1, or Gold-leg-2 in various worlds; not forced.

lg.scenario: A museum will display exactly five sculptures — Anchor, Briar, Cove, Dune, and Elm — across three consecutive wings: the North wing, the Center wing, and the South wing. The North wing holds exactly two sculptures, the Center wing holds exactly two sculptures, and the South wing holds exactly one sculpture. Within each wing the sculptures are arranged in a visible left-to-right order; we refer to the leftmost position of the North wing as North-1 and the right one as North-2, similarly for Center-1 and Center-2, with the single slot in the South wing simply called South. The display is subject to the following conditions. Cove is displayed in the North wing. Briar is displayed in the Center wing. Elm is displayed somewhere to the left of Dune (reading North-1, North-2, Center-1, Center-2, South as a single left-to-right sequence). Cove is displayed somewhere to the left of Anchor. If Anchor is displayed at North-2, then Dune is displayed in the South wing.

questions.questionStem: Which one of the following could be a complete and accurate list of the sculptures displayed at North-1, North-2, Center-1, Center-2, and South, respectively?

choices.text: Anchor, Cove, Briar, Elm, Dune

explanations.correct: Cove is at North-1 (North wing, OK), Briar is at Center-1 (Center wing, OK), Elm (pos 2) is to the left of Dune (pos 5), Cove (pos 1) is to the left of Anchor (pos 4), and Anchor is not at North-2 so the conditional is vacuously satisfied.
explanations.A: Correct. Every rule is satisfied.
explanations.B: Briar is at North-1 — but the rules require Briar to be displayed in the Center wing.
explanations.C: Cove is at South — but the rules require Cove to be in the North wing.
explanations.D: Elm is at South (position 5) and Dune is at North-2 (position 2), so Elm is not displayed to the left of Dune — violates the Elm-before-Dune rule.
explanations.E: Anchor is at North-1 (position 1) and Cove is at North-2 (position 2), so Cove is not displayed to the left of Anchor — violates the Cove-before-Anchor rule.

questions.questionStem: If Anchor is displayed at Center-1, then which one of the following must be true?

choices.text: Elm is displayed at North-1.

choices.text: Dune is displayed at Center-2.

Dune must be in the South (Elm must precede Dune and Dune has nowhere else to go that keeps Elm to its left given North is filled by Cove and one of {Elm} and Center is Anchor+Briar). Enumeration confirms Briar=Center-2 in both remaining worlds.
explanations.A: Correct. Briar must occupy Center-2 once Anchor takes Center-1.
explanations.B: Cove could be at either North-1 or North-2; not forced.
explanations.C: Elm could be at either North-1 or North-2; not forced.
explanations.D: Dune must be in the South (position 5), not Center-2.
explanations.E: Anchor is given as Center-1, not Center-2.

questions.questionStem: If Cove is displayed at North-2, then which one of the following CANNOT be true?

explanations.B: Dune in South is possible (Dune at pos 5 in several worlds with Cove at North-2).
explanations.C: Anchor in South is possible (e.g., Anchor=5, Cove=2, Elm=1, Dune=3, Briar=4).

explanations.correct: Anchor in the South wing occurs in four valid worlds (the ones where Anchor is at position 5). For example, Anchor=5, Briar=3, Cove=1, Dune=4, Elm=2.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Quinn, Ruiz, Singh, Park, Tate, Umar

explanations.correct: Ruiz at Blue-leg-1 (OK — Ruiz runs leg 1); Quinn at Blue-leg-2 (OK); Singh at Blue-leg-3 (OK — Singh runs leg 3); Park at Gold-leg-1 (OK — Park on Gold); Tate at Gold-leg-2 (Tate not at Blue leg 1, so the conditional is vacuously satisfied); Umar at Gold-leg-3.
explanations.A: Correct. Every rule is satisfied.
explanations.B: Quinn is at Gold-leg-2 — but Quinn must run leg 2 for Blue.
explanations.C: Singh is at Gold-leg-1 — but Singh must run leg 3 on whichever team she is on.
explanations.D: Ruiz is at Blue-leg-3 — but Ruiz must run leg 1 on whichever team she is on. (Also Tate at Blue-leg-1 triggers the conditional, which requires Umar at Gold-leg-3, not satisfied here either.)
explanations.E: Quinn is at Blue-leg-1 — but Quinn must run Blue-leg-2.

choices.label: A

choices.label: B

explanations.A: Correct. The conditional pins Umar to Gold-leg-3.
explanations.B: Park is at Gold-leg-2 in the surviving world, not Gold-leg-3.
explanations.C: Singh is at Blue-leg-3 in the surviving world, not Gold-leg-3.
explanations.D: Ruiz is at Gold-leg-1 in the surviving world, not Blue-leg-1 (Tate is there).
explanations.E: Park is at Gold-leg-2 in the surviving world, not Gold-leg-1.

explanations.correct: Ruiz runs leg 1 on whichever team she is on; several valid worlds place her on Gold at leg 1 (e.g., Park=5, Quinn=2, Ruiz=4, Singh=3, Tate=1, Umar=6).

explanations.B: Ruiz must run leg 1 on whichever team; Gold-leg-3 is excluded.
explanations.C: Singh must run leg 3 on whichever team; Blue-leg-1 is excluded.
explanations.D: Correct. Ruiz on Gold-leg-1 is realized in several valid worlds.
explanations.E: Quinn is pinned to Blue-leg-2.

questions.questionStem: Which one of the following must be true?

explanations.B: Park runs for Gold but could be on leg 1, leg 2, or leg 3.
explanations.C: Singh runs leg 3 but could be on either Blue or Gold.
explanations.D: Tate can run for either team in various valid worlds.
explanations.E: Umar can run for either team in various valid worlds.

explanations.A: Correct. Umar cannot be at Gold-leg-2 given Ruiz at Gold-leg-1.
explanations.B: Tate at Blue-leg-3 occurs (e.g., Park=5, Quinn=2, Ruiz=4, Singh=6, Tate=3, Umar=1).

explanations.E: Tate at Gold-leg-2 occurs (e.g., Park=6, Quinn=2, Ruiz=4, Singh=3, Tate=5, Umar=1).

lg.scenario: A small bakery produces exactly six items in a single morning — Fougasse, Ganache, Hazelnut, Iced, Jam, and Kouign — split between two product lines: Bread and Pastry. Exactly three items are baked on the Bread line and exactly three on the Pastry line. On each line the three items are baked in a strict order: Bread-batch-1 (earliest), Bread-batch-2, and Bread-batch-3; similarly Pastry-batch-1, Pastry-batch-2, and Pastry-batch-3. Each item occupies exactly one batch slot. The schedule is subject to the following conditions. Fougasse and Kouign are both on the Bread line. Ganache and Jam are both on the Pastry line. Fougasse is baked earlier than Kouign. Jam is baked earlier than Ganache. If Iced is baked as Bread-batch-2, then Hazelnut is baked as Pastry-batch-3.

questions.questionStem: Which one of the following could be the order in which the items are baked across the Bread line (batches 1 through 3) and the Pastry line (batches 1 through 3), respectively?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Fougasse, Hazelnut, Kouign, Jam, Ganache, Iced

choices.label: B
choices.text: Fougasse, Hazelnut, Kouign, Ganache, Jam, Iced

choices.label: C
choices.text: Kouign, Hazelnut, Fougasse, Jam, Ganache, Iced

choices.label: D
choices.text: Fougasse, Jam, Kouign, Hazelnut, Ganache, Iced

choices.label: E
choices.text: Ganache, Hazelnut, Kouign, Jam, Fougasse, Iced

explanations.correct: Fougasse=Bread-batch-1, Hazelnut=Bread-batch-2, Kouign=Bread-batch-3 (Fougasse before Kouign, both on Bread); Jam=Pastry-batch-1, Ganache=Pastry-batch-2 (Jam before Ganache, both on Pastry); Iced=Pastry-batch-3. Iced is not at Bread-batch-2, so the conditional is vacuously satisfied.
explanations.A: Correct. Every rule is satisfied.
explanations.B: Ganache is at Pastry-batch-1 and Jam is at Pastry-batch-2, so Jam is not baked earlier than Ganache — violates the Jam-before-Ganache rule.
explanations.C: Kouign is at Bread-batch-1 and Fougasse is at Bread-batch-3, so Fougasse is not baked earlier than Kouign — violates the Fougasse-before-Kouign rule.
explanations.D: Jam is at Bread-batch-2 — but the rules require Jam to be on the Pastry line.
explanations.E: Ganache is at Bread-batch-1 — but the rules require Ganache to be on the Pastry line.

questions.questionStem: Which one of the following CANNOT be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Kouign is baked as Pastry-batch-3.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Hazelnut is baked on the Pastry line.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Iced is baked on the Bread line.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Fougasse is baked as Bread-batch-2.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Ganache is baked as Pastry-batch-2.

explanations.correct: Kouign is fixed to the Bread line by rule, so Kouign can never be a Pastry batch.
explanations.A: Correct. Kouign must be on Bread.
explanations.B: Hazelnut on Pastry occurs in several valid worlds (e.g., Hazelnut at Pastry-batch-3).
explanations.C: Iced on Bread occurs in several valid worlds (e.g., Iced at Bread-batch-3).
explanations.D: Fougasse at Bread-batch-2 occurs (e.g., Fougasse=2, Ganache=5, Hazelnut=1, Iced=6, Jam=4, Kouign=3).
explanations.E: Ganache at Pastry-batch-2 (position 5) occurs in many worlds.

questions.questionStem: Which one of the following could be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Jam is baked on the Bread line.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Iced is baked as Pastry-batch-1.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ganache is baked earlier than Jam.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Kouign is baked as Pastry-batch-2.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Fougasse is baked as Bread-batch-3.

explanations.correct: Iced at Pastry-batch-1 (position 4) occurs in multiple worlds (e.g., Fougasse=1, Ganache=6, Hazelnut=3, Iced=4, Jam=5, Kouign=2).
explanations.A: Jam is fixed to Pastry by rule.
explanations.B: Correct. Iced on Pastry-batch-1 is realized in several valid worlds.
explanations.C: Jam must be earlier than Ganache by rule.
explanations.D: Kouign is fixed to Bread by rule.
explanations.E: Fougasse must be earlier than Kouign. With both on Bread and three Bread slots, Fougasse at Bread-batch-3 would leave no later Bread slot for Kouign.

questions.questionStem: If Iced is baked as Bread-batch-1, then which one of the following must be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Fougasse is baked as Bread-batch-2.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Hazelnut is baked as Pastry-batch-3.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Jam is baked as Pastry-batch-1.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Ganache is baked as Pastry-batch-3.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Hazelnut is baked as Pastry-batch-2.

explanations.correct: With Iced filling Bread-batch-1, the other two Bread slots must go to Fougasse and Kouign in that order (Fougasse before Kouign). Fougasse is therefore forced to Bread-batch-2 and Kouign to Bread-batch-3 in every surviving world.
explanations.A: Correct. Fougasse must be at Bread-batch-2 in every surviving world.
explanations.B: Hazelnut is at Pastry-batch-3 in only one of the three surviving worlds; not forced.
explanations.C: Jam is at Pastry-batch-1 in two of three surviving worlds, but not all; not forced.
explanations.D: Ganache is at Pastry-batch-3 in two of three surviving worlds, but not all; not forced.
explanations.E: Hazelnut is at Pastry-batch-2 in only one of the three surviving worlds; not forced.

questions.questionStem: If Hazelnut is baked as Bread-batch-1, then which one of the following CANNOT be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Iced is baked on the Bread line.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Fougasse is baked as Bread-batch-2.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Kouign is baked as Bread-batch-3.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Ganache is baked as Pastry-batch-3.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Jam is baked as Pastry-batch-2.

explanations.correct: If Hazelnut occupies Bread-batch-1, then the remaining two Bread slots must be filled by Fougasse and Kouign (in that order). Iced must therefore be on the Pastry line in every surviving world.
explanations.A: Correct. With Hazelnut at Bread-batch-1, Iced cannot be on Bread.
explanations.B: Fougasse at Bread-batch-2 is realized (e.g., Fougasse=2, Ganache=5, Hazelnut=1, Iced=6, Jam=4, Kouign=3).
explanations.C: Kouign at Bread-batch-3 is realized in all surviving worlds.
explanations.D: Ganache at Pastry-batch-3 (position 6) is realized in most surviving worlds.
explanations.E: Jam at Pastry-batch-2 (position 5) is realized in some surviving worlds.

lg.scenario: A town parade features exactly seven floats — Aster, Bluebell, Calla, Daisy, Edelweiss, Foxglove, and Gentian — assembled into two district contingents: District A and District B. District A contains exactly four floats, arranged in marching order from A-1 (first to pass the reviewing stand) through A-4, and District B contains exactly three floats, arranged in order from B-1 through B-3. Reading A-1, A-2, A-3, A-4, B-1, B-2, B-3 as a single early-to-late sequence, each float occupies exactly one slot. The arrangement is subject to the following conditions. Aster is in District A. Calla is in District A. Bluebell is in District B. Daisy is in District B. Aster marches at A-1. Bluebell marches earlier than Daisy. Calla marches earlier than Edelweiss. If Foxglove marches in District A, then Gentian marches in District B. If Gentian marches at A-1, then Edelweiss marches at A-3.

questions.questionStem: Which one of the following could be a complete and accurate list of the floats marching at A-1, A-2, A-3, A-4, B-1, B-2, and B-3, respectively?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Aster, Calla, Edelweiss, Foxglove, Bluebell, Daisy, Gentian

choices.label: B
choices.text: Calla, Aster, Edelweiss, Foxglove, Bluebell, Daisy, Gentian

choices.label: C
choices.text: Aster, Edelweiss, Calla, Foxglove, Bluebell, Daisy, Gentian

choices.label: D
choices.text: Aster, Calla, Edelweiss, Foxglove, Daisy, Bluebell, Gentian

choices.label: E
choices.text: Aster, Calla, Edelweiss, Bluebell, Foxglove, Daisy, Gentian

explanations.correct: Aster at A-1 (rule), Calla at A-2 (District A), Edelweiss at A-3 (Calla-before-Edelweiss satisfied), Foxglove at A-4 (District A). Because Foxglove is in District A, the conditional requires Gentian in District B — Gentian is at B-3. Bluebell at B-1 and Daisy at B-2 satisfy Bluebell-before-Daisy.
explanations.A: Correct. Every rule is satisfied.
explanations.B: Aster is at A-2 — but Aster must march at A-1.
explanations.C: Edelweiss is at A-2 and Calla is at A-3, so Calla does not march earlier than Edelweiss — violates the Calla-before-Edelweiss rule.
explanations.D: Daisy is at B-1 and Bluebell is at B-2, so Bluebell does not march earlier than Daisy — violates the Bluebell-before-Daisy rule.
explanations.E: Bluebell is at A-4 — but Bluebell must march in District B.

questions.questionStem: If Foxglove marches at A-2, then which one of the following must be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Edelweiss marches at A-4.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Bluebell marches at B-1.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Gentian marches at B-1.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Daisy marches at B-2.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Calla marches at A-4.

explanations.correct: With Foxglove at A-2 (District A), the conditional forces Gentian into District B. Aster is at A-1, so A-3 and A-4 must go to Calla and Edelweiss. Because Calla must march earlier than Edelweiss, Calla takes A-3 and Edelweiss takes A-4 in every one of the three surviving worlds.
explanations.A: Correct. Edelweiss is forced to A-4 in all three surviving worlds.
explanations.B: Bluebell could be at B-1 or B-2; not forced.
explanations.C: Gentian could be at B-1, B-2, or B-3; not forced.
explanations.D: Daisy could be at B-2 or B-3; not forced.
explanations.E: Calla is forced to A-3, not A-4.

questions.questionStem: Which one of the following CANNOT be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Daisy marches at B-1.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Foxglove marches at B-1.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Gentian marches at A-2.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Edelweiss marches at A-3.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Calla marches at A-3.

explanations.correct: Bluebell must march earlier than Daisy, and both are in District B. Bluebell must therefore occupy a District B slot earlier than Daisy, so Daisy cannot be the first District B float (B-1).
explanations.A: Correct. Bluebell must precede Daisy within District B, so Daisy at B-1 is impossible.
explanations.B: Foxglove at B-1 (position 5) occurs in several valid worlds (e.g., Foxglove=5, Gentian=4).
explanations.C: Gentian at A-2 occurs in valid worlds (e.g., Calla=3, Edelweiss=4, Foxglove=6 or 7, Gentian=2).
explanations.D: Edelweiss at A-3 occurs in many valid worlds (e.g., Calla=2, Edelweiss=3).
explanations.E: Calla at A-3 occurs in several valid worlds (e.g., Calla=3, Edelweiss=4, Foxglove=2).

questions.questionStem: If Gentian marches at A-2, then which one of the following could be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Edelweiss marches at A-3.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Foxglove marches at B-1.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Calla marches at A-2.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Daisy marches at B-1.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Aster marches at A-2.

explanations.correct: With Gentian at A-2 (District A), the Foxglove conditional contrapositive tells us Foxglove cannot be in District A (otherwise Gentian would have to be in District B). So Foxglove is in District B. In the surviving worlds Foxglove takes B-1, B-2, or B-3 depending on Bluebell and Daisy. In particular, Foxglove at B-1 occurs in a valid surviving world (Bluebell=B-2, Daisy=B-3, Foxglove=B-1).
explanations.A: Edelweiss is forced to A-4: with Aster at A-1 and Gentian at A-2, Calla and Edelweiss must fill A-3 and A-4, and Calla must precede Edelweiss, so Edelweiss is at A-4.
explanations.B: Correct. Foxglove at B-1 occurs in a valid surviving world.
explanations.C: Calla is forced to A-3; Calla at A-2 is impossible because Gentian occupies A-2.
explanations.D: Bluebell must precede Daisy within District B, so Daisy cannot be at B-1.
explanations.E: Aster is pinned to A-1 by rule; Aster cannot be at A-2.

questions.questionStem: Which one of the following must be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Edelweiss marches in District A.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Foxglove marches in District A.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Gentian marches in District B.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Calla marches at A-2.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Daisy marches at B-3.

explanations.correct: Aster is at A-1 and Bluebell and Daisy fill two of the three District B slots. That leaves five floats (Calla, Edelweiss, Foxglove, Gentian, and one of {Bluebell/Daisy's B-slot mate}) to fill three District A slots and one District B slot. Because Calla is in District A and Calla must march earlier than Edelweiss, Edelweiss must be at a position later than Calla. Solver enumeration of all valid worlds confirms that Edelweiss always lands at A-3 or A-4 — never in District B.
explanations.A: Correct. Edelweiss is in District A in every one of the 18 valid worlds.
explanations.B: Foxglove is in District B in multiple valid worlds (e.g., Foxglove=5, 6, or 7).
explanations.C: Gentian is in District A in multiple valid worlds (e.g., Gentian=2, 3, or 4).
explanations.D: Calla is at A-3 in several valid worlds, not always A-2.
explanations.E: Daisy is at B-2 in some valid worlds, not always B-3.

lg.scenario: A one-day academic conference features exactly seven talks — given by Patel, Quon, Rao, Silva, Torres, Udo, and Vega — split between two tracks: Morning and Afternoon. The Morning track holds exactly four talks, ordered from M-1 (earliest) through M-4 (latest), and the Afternoon track holds exactly three talks, ordered from A-1 (earliest) through A-3 (latest). Reading M-1, M-2, M-3, M-4, A-1, A-2, A-3 as a single early-to-late sequence, each speaker gives exactly one talk. The schedule is subject to the following conditions. Patel, Silva, and Torres all present in the Morning track. Quon and Rao both present in the Afternoon track. Silva presents earlier than Torres. Patel presents earlier than Silva. Quon presents earlier than Rao. Torres presents at M-4. If Udo presents in the Morning track, then Vega presents in the Afternoon track. If Vega presents at M-1, then Rao presents at A-3.

questions.questionStem: Which one of the following could be a complete and accurate list of the speakers presenting at M-1, M-2, M-3, M-4, A-1, A-2, and A-3, respectively?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Patel, Silva, Udo, Torres, Quon, Rao, Vega

choices.label: B
choices.text: Patel, Silva, Udo, Torres, Rao, Quon, Vega

choices.label: C
choices.text: Silva, Patel, Udo, Torres, Quon, Rao, Vega

choices.label: D
choices.text: Vega, Patel, Silva, Torres, Quon, Rao, Udo

choices.label: E
choices.text: Patel, Silva, Torres, Udo, Quon, Rao, Vega

explanations.correct: Patel at M-1 (Morning, earlier than Silva), Silva at M-2 (Morning, earlier than Torres), Udo at M-3 (Udo in Morning, so conditional forces Vega to Afternoon — Vega at A-3 satisfies that), Torres at M-4 (rule), Quon at A-1 (earlier than Rao), Rao at A-2, Vega at A-3. Every rule is satisfied.
explanations.A: Correct. Every rule is satisfied.
explanations.B: Rao is at A-1 and Quon is at A-2, so Quon does not present earlier than Rao — violates the Quon-before-Rao rule.
explanations.C: Silva is at M-1 and Patel is at M-2, so Patel does not present earlier than Silva — violates the Patel-before-Silva rule.
explanations.D: Vega is at M-1 but Rao is at A-2 — the conditional 'If Vega presents at M-1, then Rao presents at A-3' is violated.
explanations.E: Torres is at M-3 — but Torres must present at M-4.

questions.questionStem: If Udo presents at M-3, then which one of the following must be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Silva presents at M-2.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Vega presents at A-3.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Quon presents at A-1.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Rao presents at A-2.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Patel presents at M-2.

explanations.correct: With Udo at M-3 and Torres at M-4, the remaining Morning slots (M-1 and M-2) must go to Patel and Silva. Patel must present earlier than Silva, so Patel occupies M-1 and Silva occupies M-2 in every surviving world.
explanations.A: Correct. Silva is at M-2 in all three surviving worlds.
explanations.B: Vega could be at A-1, A-2, or A-3 across the three surviving worlds; not forced.
explanations.C: Quon could be at A-1 or A-2 in the surviving worlds; not forced.
explanations.D: Rao could be at A-2 or A-3 in the surviving worlds; not forced.
explanations.E: Patel is forced to M-1, not M-2 (Silva occupies M-2).

questions.questionStem: Which one of the following CANNOT be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Quon presents at A-3.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Udo presents at M-1.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Vega presents at A-1.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Silva presents at M-3.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Rao presents at A-2.

explanations.correct: Quon must present earlier than Rao, and both are in the Afternoon track. The Afternoon track has only three slots (A-1, A-2, A-3). For Quon to be earlier than Rao, Quon cannot occupy A-3 (the last Afternoon slot) — otherwise there would be no later slot for Rao.
explanations.A: Correct. Quon at A-3 would leave no later Afternoon slot for Rao.
explanations.B: Udo at M-1 occurs in several valid worlds (e.g., Patel=2, Udo=1).
explanations.C: Vega at A-1 (position 5) occurs in several valid worlds (e.g., Udo=6, Vega=5, Patel=2).
explanations.D: Silva at M-3 occurs in many valid worlds (e.g., Patel=1 or 2, Silva=3).
explanations.E: Rao at A-2 (position 6) occurs in many valid worlds.

questions.questionStem: Which one of the following could be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Vega presents at M-1.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Udo presents in the Morning track and Vega presents in the Morning track.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Patel presents at M-3.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Silva presents in the Afternoon track.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Torres presents at M-3.

explanations.correct: Vega at M-1 (position 1) occurs in two valid worlds (e.g., Patel=2, Quon=5, Rao=7, Silva=3, Torres=4, Udo=6, Vega=1). When Vega is at M-1 the second conditional forces Rao to A-3, which is consistent with the other rules.
explanations.A: Correct. Vega at M-1 is realized in valid worlds.
explanations.B: If Udo is in Morning, the first conditional forces Vega to Afternoon — they cannot both be in Morning.
explanations.C: Patel must present earlier than Silva, and Torres is pinned at M-4. If Patel were at M-3, Silva would need a later Morning slot, but M-4 is Torres's. Impossible.
explanations.D: Silva must present in the Morning track by rule.
explanations.E: Torres is pinned to M-4 by rule.

questions.questionStem: If Vega presents at M-2, then which one of the following CANNOT be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Silva presents at M-2.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Udo presents at A-1.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Quon presents at A-1.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Rao presents at A-3.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Silva presents at M-3.

explanations.correct: With Vega at M-2, Vega occupies M-2 exclusively. Silva cannot also be at M-2. Moreover, Patel must precede Silva and Torres is at M-4, so Silva is forced to M-3 in every surviving world.
explanations.A: Correct. Vega occupies M-2, so Silva cannot be at M-2.
explanations.B: Udo at A-1 (position 5) occurs in one surviving world (Patel=1, Quon=6, Rao=7, Silva=3, Udo=5, Vega=2).
explanations.C: Quon at A-1 occurs in surviving worlds (e.g., Patel=1, Quon=5, Rao=6 or 7).
explanations.D: Rao at A-3 occurs in surviving worlds (e.g., Patel=1, Quon=5, Rao=7, Udo=6, Vega=2).
explanations.E: Silva at M-3 is in fact forced in every surviving world — so it must be true (and therefore could be true).

lg.scenario: A small library is reshelving exactly six books — Aurora, Bronte, Clio, Delphi, Eureka, and Fermi — across three wings: the Fiction wing (exactly two books, shelved left-to-right as F-1 and F-2), the History wing (exactly two books, shelved left-to-right as H-1 and H-2), and the Science wing (exactly two books, shelved left-to-right as S-1 and S-2). Reading F-1, F-2, H-1, H-2, S-1, S-2 as a single left-to-right sequence, each book occupies exactly one slot. The reshelving is subject to the following conditions. Aurora is in the Fiction wing. Clio is in the History wing. Fermi is in the Science wing. Bronte is shelved somewhere to the left of Eureka in the overall left-to-right sequence. If Bronte is in the Fiction wing, then Delphi is in the Science wing. If Delphi is at F-1, then Eureka is at S-1.

questions.questionStem: Which one of the following could be a complete and accurate list of the books shelved at F-1, F-2, H-1, H-2, S-1, and S-2, respectively?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Aurora, Bronte, Clio, Eureka, Delphi, Fermi

choices.label: B
choices.text: Aurora, Clio, Bronte, Eureka, Delphi, Fermi

choices.label: C
choices.text: Aurora, Eureka, Clio, Bronte, Delphi, Fermi

choices.label: D
choices.text: Aurora, Bronte, Clio, Fermi, Delphi, Eureka

choices.label: E
choices.text: Aurora, Bronte, Delphi, Clio, Eureka, Fermi

explanations.correct: Aurora at F-1 (Fiction), Bronte at F-2 (Fiction — so the conditional requires Delphi in Science, and Delphi is at S-1: satisfied), Clio at H-1 (History), Eureka at H-2 (Bronte at position 2 is left of Eureka at position 4), Delphi at S-1 (Delphi not at F-1, so the second conditional is vacuous), Fermi at S-2 (Science).
explanations.A: Correct. Every rule is satisfied.
explanations.B: Clio is at F-2 — but Clio must be shelved in the History wing.
explanations.C: Bronte is at H-2 (position 4) and Eureka is at F-2 (position 2), so Bronte is not shelved to the left of Eureka — violates the Bronte-before-Eureka rule.
explanations.D: Fermi is at H-2 — but Fermi must be shelved in the Science wing.
explanations.E: Bronte is in Fiction (F-2) but Delphi is at H-1, not in Science — violates the conditional 'If Bronte is in Fiction, then Delphi is in Science.'

questions.questionStem: If Bronte is shelved at F-2, then which one of the following must be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Aurora is shelved at F-1.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Clio is shelved at H-1.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Eureka is shelved at H-1.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Delphi is shelved at S-1.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Fermi is shelved at S-2.

explanations.correct: With Bronte at F-2, the only remaining Fiction slot is F-1, and Aurora must be in the Fiction wing — so Aurora must be at F-1 in every surviving world.
explanations.A: Correct. Aurora is at F-1 in all four surviving worlds.
explanations.B: Clio could be at H-1 or H-2 across the surviving worlds; not forced.
explanations.C: Eureka could be at H-1 or H-2; not forced.
explanations.D: Delphi could be at S-1 or S-2 (both Science); not forced.
explanations.E: Fermi could be at S-1 or S-2; not forced.

questions.questionStem: If Delphi is shelved at F-1, then which one of the following could be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Eureka is shelved at S-2.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Clio is shelved at H-1.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Aurora is shelved at F-1.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Bronte is shelved at F-2.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Fermi is shelved at S-1.

explanations.correct: With Delphi at F-1, the second conditional forces Eureka to S-1 (position 5). Aurora must be in Fiction and F-1 is taken, so Aurora is at F-2. Fermi must be in Science and S-1 is taken, so Fermi is at S-2. Bronte must be left of Eureka (position 5), so Bronte is at position 3 or 4 (History). Clio must be in History and takes whichever History slot Bronte leaves. In one of the two surviving worlds Bronte is at H-2 (position 4) and Clio is at H-1 (position 3), which realizes choice B.
explanations.A: Eureka is forced to S-1 (position 5) by the conditional; Eureka at S-2 is impossible in this case.
explanations.B: Correct. Clio at H-1 occurs in one of the two surviving worlds.
explanations.C: Aurora is forced to F-2 (Delphi occupies F-1); Aurora at F-1 is impossible.
explanations.D: Bronte must be at position 3 or 4 (History wing) in the surviving worlds; Bronte at F-2 is impossible.
explanations.E: Fermi is forced to S-2 (Eureka occupies S-1); Fermi at S-1 is impossible.

questions.questionStem: Which one of the following CANNOT be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Fermi is shelved at H-1.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Delphi is shelved at F-1.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Bronte is shelved at H-2.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Eureka is shelved at H-1.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Aurora is shelved at F-2.

explanations.correct: Fermi must be shelved in the Science wing (S-1 or S-2) by rule, so Fermi at H-1 is impossible.
explanations.A: Correct. Fermi must be in the Science wing.
explanations.B: Delphi at F-1 occurs in valid worlds (e.g., Delphi=1, Eureka=5).
explanations.C: Bronte at H-2 occurs in valid worlds (e.g., Bronte=4, Clio=3, Delphi=2).
explanations.D: Eureka at H-1 (position 3) occurs in valid worlds (e.g., Clio=4, Eureka=3).
explanations.E: Aurora at F-2 occurs in valid worlds (e.g., Aurora=2, Bronte=1).

questions.questionStem: If Eureka is shelved at H-1, then which one of the following must be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Clio is shelved at H-2.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Bronte is shelved at F-1.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Delphi is shelved at S-1.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Fermi is shelved at S-2.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Aurora is shelved at F-1.

explanations.correct: With Eureka at H-1 (position 3), Clio must still be in the History wing. The only other History slot is H-2, so Clio must be at H-2 in every surviving world.
explanations.A: Correct. Clio is forced to H-2 in all four surviving worlds.
explanations.B: Bronte could be at F-1 or F-2 in the surviving worlds; not forced.
explanations.C: Delphi could be at S-1 or S-2; not forced.
explanations.D: Fermi could be at S-1 or S-2; not forced.
explanations.E: Aurora could be at F-1 or F-2; not forced.
